Start with a business decision, then ask what you need to measure, predict, test, optimize, or verify. # Applied labs

All three labs use fictional data. Each ends with a business recommendation you can defend using the output. Run the scripts from the repository root, or open the notebook in JupyterLab as described in the [setup](../README.md#run-the-labs).

| Lab | Business decision | What to practice |
|---|---|---|
| [01 · Campaign decision](01_campaign_decision.ipynb) | Should Alder Market replace its current discount email with AI-written copy? | Screen the copy, estimate incremental purchases, compare lift with break-even and an unsubscribe limit, and score model responses against six decision scenarios. |
| [02 · Inventory decision](02_inventory_decision.py) | How many units should a retailer stock next week? | Compare chronological forecasting baselines, estimate demand uncertainty from earlier errors, and evaluate the full decision with shortage and overstock costs. |
| [03 · Grounded policy Q&A](03_grounded_policy_qa.py) | Can a business assistant answer a policy question from the evidence available? | Compare lexical retrieval with date and scope checks. Inspect when retrieval selects an irrelevant policy and when the assistant should abstain. |

## What to try after each run

1. **Campaign.** Change one economic input in the notebook and calculate the new decision before running it. Then choose a real randomized dataset from the [online guide](../resources/ONLINE.md#datasets-and-notebooks-for-practice). Define the estimand and reproduce the baseline comparison before trying an uplift model.
2. **Inventory.** Run `python3 labs/02_inventory_decision.py --underage-cost 18` to double the cost of unmet demand. How does the order quantity change? Keep model selection and cost tuning out of the final evaluation period. Write down which operational assumption would make the exercise's independent weekly decisions unrealistic.
3. **Policy.** Add an expired policy whose wording exactly matches the question, then add a case with an unspecified sales channel. Score evidence applicability and abstention separately. A language model is an optional extension. Keep deterministic tests for scope and effective dates.

For each lab, summarize the **incumbent**, **metric**, **result**, **limitation**, and **next action** in five sentences. The [topic index](../learning/TOPIC_INDEX.md) points to more examples and data.

# Business analytics studio cases

These original case briefs are for AI scientists and business-school instructors preparing a class exercise or capstone. Use a case to practice making and defending a business decision with AI, data, and a credible comparison. Each brief gives a manageable starting point, a test that can fail, and an extension. The [teaching map](TEACHING_MAP.md) connects the methods to business-school curricula. Use [datasets and benchmarks](../resources/DATASETS.md) when you want to extend a case with public data.

| Business decision | Analytics to practice | Starting material |
|---|---|---|
| [Which email should we send?](#marketing-campaign-rollout) | Experimentation and unit economics | Campaign notebook |
| [How much inventory should we order?](#operations-inventory-planning) | Probabilistic forecasting and optimization | Inventory script |
| [Which deals should the sales team review?](#sales-pipeline-triage) | Prediction, capacity, and evaluation by cohort | Fictional multi-table CRM dataset |
| [Which transactions need a reviewer?](#accounting-review-queue) | Selective classification and exception review | Instructor-created synthetic ledger |
| [Can we trust the weekly KPI report?](#business-intelligence-kpi-reporting) | SQL, data reconciliation, and grounded answers | Small instructor-created warehouse |
| [When should support escalate?](#customer-service-policy-triage) | Retrieval, abstention, and evaluation of workflow quality | Grounded policy script |

## Marketing campaign rollout

The growth manager must decide whether to replace the current discount email, run a larger experiment, or keep the current campaign. Use the randomized comparison in the campaign notebook to estimate incremental purchases with uncertainty. Convert lift into expected incremental contribution using margin, incremental cost, and eligible audience size. Check the unsubscribe guardrail before recommending a rollout. Extend the exercise by comparing a pre-specified customer segment or changing one economic assumption. Ask which change would reverse the recommendation. A published online retail study provides a field comparison across seven AI-assisted workflows, including evidence on where sales effects varied. [Campaign notebook](../labs/01_campaign_decision.ipynb) · [Fang et al., *Management Science*, 2026](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2026.00623)

## Operations inventory planning

A replenishment planner needs an order for next week. Compare the current order rule with a seasonal forecast and a demand-quantile rule tuned on earlier periods. Hold out the latest weeks and assess forecasting error alongside shortage cost, overstock cost, and service level. Stress-test the recommended order when underage cost rises or a promotion shifts demand. Extend the case with a storage constraint across two products. Keep planned events available to both forecasting methods and document which event dates were known when ordering. [Inventory script](../labs/02_inventory_decision.py) · [Forecast validation and interval examples, OTexts, 2026](https://otexts.com/fpppy/05-toolbox.html)

Wharton’s Spencer’s and Spirit Halloween project write-up reports a held-out season comparison for licensed merchandise. Ask students what follow-up would test the projected margin benefit and how they would measure stockouts when sales are all they observe. [Wharton case study, 2025](https://ai-analytics.wharton.upenn.edu/student-programs/analytics-accelerator/license%E2%80%91level-demand-forecasting-for-spencers-spirit-halloween/)

## Sales pipeline triage

A sales manager can review only a fixed number of opportunities each Monday. Compare an incumbent prioritization rule with a simple model for near-term wins using the fictional Maven CRM data. Score held-out periods, report precision among the opportunities the team can review, and audit calibration and errors by account segment. Build features from fields available at the scoring time. Where the public extract lacks historical stage changes, reconstruct an earlier view from defensible recorded timestamps or simulate snapshots and label them. Use the result to prioritize outreach or review for a pilot. Measuring incremental wins from that outreach requires a separate comparison. [Maven Sales Challenge, 2024](https://mavenanalytics.io/challenges/maven-sales-challenge)

## Accounting review queue

A controller needs to decide which expense lines can be pre-classified and which should be sent to a reviewer. Build a fictional ledger and chart of accounts with examples of ambiguous vendors, missing documentation, refunds, and policy changes. Compare a rules baseline with a text classifier or document-grounded model. Use a held-out batch to score false approvals, coverage at the proposed review threshold, and reviewer workload. Require a source reference for each suggestion and define when to defer. Extend by comparing performance on familiar and new vendors. Choi and Xie’s paper includes a randomized transaction-classification exercise with accountants and provides a reference for assessing how people respond to model suggestions. [Choi and Xie, *Journal of Accounting Research*, 2026](https://doi.org/10.1111/1475-679X.70052)

## Business intelligence KPI reporting

An operations director wants a weekly report of net sales and returns by channel. Give teams small fictional tables for orders, line items, and refunds, a metric dictionary, and a set of reference SQL queries. Compare a self-service dashboard or saved query workflow with an assistant that reads the same definitions and produces queries or explanations. Score result accuracy, business interpretation, and traceability separately. Include cases with a one-to-many join, a late refund, different order and refund dates, and an undefined denominator. Ask students to reconcile one answer against the source rows and specify when the assistant should request clarification. DataSpace offers a recent benchmark for evaluating whether data agents return complete, verifiable results across different source types. [Li et al., DataSpace preprint, 2026](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2608.03451)

## Customer service policy triage

A support manager must decide when a proposed assistant should answer, ask for context, or escalate. Use the policy lab to compare keyword matching with a workflow that checks channel, effective date, and applicability. Score supported answers, inappropriate answers, and correct escalation separately. Add ambiguous requests and policy revisions to a held-out set. Estimate review workload and missed escalations at the proposed operating point. Extend the case by drafting a pilot with repeat-contact rate and resolution quality alongside throughput. A published field study of a phased support rollout offers a comparison between a real operating outcome and the measures available in the simulation. [Grounded policy script](../labs/03_grounded_policy_qa.py) · [Brynjolfsson, Li, and Raymond, *Quarterly Journal of Economics*, 2025](https://doi.org/10.1093/qje/qjae044)

## Common submission and rubric

Ask for a **one-page decision memo**, a **reproducible analysis**, and a **short demonstration**. The memo names the decision owner, available actions, recommendation, evidence, uncertainty, and conditions for changing the recommendation. The demonstration reproduces one important calculation and explains an error or borderline case. Teams can use a spreadsheet, SQL, a Python notebook, or another tool that lets the reviewer trace and reproduce the result.

| Criterion | Evidence that meets it |
|---|---|
| Decision framing | The memo defines the decision, population, business outcome, operating constraints, and the current process or rule. |
| Data and measurement | The analysis states the unit, time window, source, and metric denominator. It documents join keys, exclusions, and what information would have been available at the decision time. |
| Comparison and uncertainty | The incumbent and candidate receive the same eligible inputs and evaluation conditions. The test design matches the claim, such as a holdout for prediction or a credible counterfactual for incremental impact. Results show variation or uncertainty relevant to the decision. |
| Business value and controls | The memo translates errors or effects into plausible costs, workload, margin, or service outcomes. It states when to defer, stop, or escalate, and how the owner would check results after a rollout. |
| Reproducibility and communication | A reviewer can rerun or inspect the pivotal result from documented data and steps. The team can explain one failure and identify what additional evidence would change its recommendation. |

For a short exercise, assess each criterion as **demonstrated**, **partly demonstrated**, or **needs evidence**. Share the rubric and acceptance thresholds before students evaluate the final cases. Credit alternative methods that support the same claim. A recommendation to retain the incumbent or collect more evidence can meet all criteria.

For a reproducible handoff, record the data release or synthetic generation procedure, split and exclusion rules, environment or formulas, and where to find the benchmark outputs. An AI system should also record the model identifier, prompts, retrieval corpus version, available tools, and the outputs actually scored. Where runs vary, repeat selected cases and summarize the spread. Use case-level notes to distinguish an arithmetic error, unsupported result, invalid input, and appropriate abstention. [Stanford CS 329Z project brief, Fall 2026](https://cs329z.stanford.edu/project.html)

## Public practicum examples

- **Georgia Tech Scheller, Business Analytics Practicum (Fall 2026).** The syllabus shows how graduate teams move from a sponsor’s question through data readiness, method selection, and an evidence-based recommendation. Its project directions include BI, operational analytics, text analytics, and generative AI. Use its project lifecycle to scope a sponsor engagement. [MGT 6214 syllabus](https://syllabus.gatech.edu/sites/default/files/2026-05/MGT_6214_Syllabus_Fan_0.pdf)
- **University of Rochester Simon, Online Business Analytics Capstone Project (2026–27).** The catalog describes a multi-source case and a consulting deliverable for executive stakeholders. Use that format to require a recommendation supported by quantitative evidence, even when a client dataset is unavailable. [GBA 475P catalog entry](https://simon.rochester.edu/file/27468/download?token=FJX1u1Gv)
- **National University of Singapore, Business Analytics Capstone (2026–27 project periods).** The public sponsor page describes how deliverables differ across agentic AI, dashboards, and advanced analytics. It gives activity and deliverable examples for choosing the method after seeing the business problem and data. [Capstone scope and examples](https://www.comp.nus.edu.sg/industry/capstone-projects/)
- **Wharton AI & Analytics Accelerator (Fall 2026).** The public sponsor briefs include evaluation of a multimodal travel agent and forecasting returns on enterprise AI. They provide examples of framing evaluation criteria around how someone will use the work. Sponsors arrange data access for participating students. [Project briefs](https://ai-analytics.wharton.upenn.edu/for-students/ai-analytics-accelerator/#fall-2026-ai-analytics-accelerator-projects)

# AI in business analytics by function

Find examples by business function or use the question map to choose an analytical approach.

For research evidence behind each use case, see [applied research by function](../resources/BUSINESS_APPLICATIONS.md). For practice with public data, see [datasets and benchmarks](../resources/DATASETS.md).

## Where the methods show up

| Business function | Decisions and measures | Common pitfall | Cases, data, and practice |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Marketing and growth** | Target offers, test creative, and allocate spend. Track incremental conversion, contribution, retention, and customer lifetime value. | Confusing likely buyers with buyers persuaded by the offer. | [Campaign decision lab](../labs/01_campaign_decision.ipynb), [Wharton–Petco email case](https://ai-analytics.wharton.upenn.edu/student-programs/analytics-accelerator/optimizing-petcos-email-marketing-strategy-using-generative-ai/), [Google Meridian budget optimization](https://developers.google.com/meridian/notebook) |
| **Sales** | Prioritize accounts, assess pipeline coverage, and forecast booked revenue. Track win rate, deal cycle, and forecast calibration. | Training on deal outcomes or stage changes that would be unknown when the prediction is made. | [2024 Maven Sales Challenge](https://mavenanalytics.io/challenges/maven-sales-challenge) (fictional CRM data) |
| **Operations and supply chain** | Allocate inventory, staffing, or capacity. Track service level, stockouts, total cost, forecast bias, and throughput. | Choosing the most accurate demand forecast without checking stockout and overstock costs. | [Inventory decision lab](../labs/02_inventory_decision.py), [MIT Sloan Cemex case](https://mitsloan.mit.edu/teaching-resources-library/cemex-journey-to-ai-scale), [Forecasting and operational decisions books](../resources/BOOKS.md#forecasting-and-operational-decisions) |
| **Finance and risk** | Forecast cash flow, evaluate credit risk, or compare operating scenarios. Check forecast error, calibration, and the costs of missed or false alerts. | Mixing reporting periods or accepting a generated number without reconciling it to the filing. | [Recent SEC financial statement data](https://www.sec.gov/dera/data/financial-statement-data-sets.html), [Southampton AI in Finance course](../resources/COURSES.md#finance-and-risk) |
| **Accounting and audit** | Classify transactions, reconcile records, and route exceptions to reviewers. Track reconciliation accuracy, false approvals, and audit coverage. | Letting an AI-generated classification determine approval without a traceable control. | [Human + AI in Accounting study](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/1475-679x.70052), [Governance research](../resources/RESEARCH.md#evaluation-and-governance) |
| **Customer service** | Route cases and decide where an assistant should answer, abstain, or escalate. Track resolution, repeat contact, satisfaction, and policy accuracy. | Optimizing first-response speed while repeat contacts rise. | [Grounded policy Q&A lab](../labs/03_grounded_policy_qa.py), [Customer-support field study](https://doi.org/10.1093/qje/qjae044), [Practice datasets](../resources/ONLINE.md#datasets-and-notebooks-for-practice) |
| **Product and strategy** | Select AI use cases and decide whether to expand a pilot. Track adoption, task success, incremental value, and total cost. | Treating prototype quality as evidence that users will pay, switch, or keep using it. | [BYU Marriott product studio](https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/), [Implementation cases](../resources/ONLINE.md#how-businesses-and-business-schools-use-ai), [Strategy and adoption books](../resources/BOOKS.md#strategy-adoption-and-governance) |
| **People and organization** | Redesign team roles and training for AI-assisted work. Track output quality, workload, learning, retention, and differences across groups. | Generalizing results from early adopters to workers with different tasks or experience. | [P&G teamwork experiment](https://doi.org/10.1287/orsc.2025.20702), [Studies of AI at work](../resources/RESEARCH.md#organizations-and-real-work) |

## Choose a method by question

| Question | Typical methods | Evidence and example |
|---|---|---|
| What happened? | SQL, BI, metric trees, visualization, cohorts | Reconcile the underlying counts and show where conversion changed. |
| What is likely to happen? | Forecasting, regression, classification, anomaly detection | Validate on held-out data that reflect the decision horizon. Estimate next week's demand or a customer's churn risk. |
| What would change if we acted? | A/B experiments, quasi-experiments, causal ML, uplift | Define the comparison and evaluate identification assumptions. Estimate how many extra purchases a promotion caused. |
| What should we do? | Decision analysis, simulation, optimization, thresholds | Model costs, constraints, and uncertainty. Allocate ad spend or inventory subject to budget and service constraints. |
| What can AI read, generate, or execute? | NLP, embeddings, retrieval, structured generation, tool use, agents | Compare with the current workflow and test evidence, accuracy, costs, abstention, and actions. Extract themes from reviews or route support tickets. |

See the [working glossary](GLOSSARY.md) for definitions and the [business-school teaching map](TEACHING_MAP.md) for course examples.

# Business analytics for scientists

Business analytics uses data to understand performance, predict outcomes, and evaluate decisions. As a scientist, you bring experience defining variables, testing hypotheses, quantifying uncertainty, and documenting assumptions. In business, those skills support a decision someone owns, such as whether to send an offer, order more stock, or let an AI assistant answer a customer. The quality of the recommendation depends on data definitions, economic consequences, and how the decision will be carried out.

## How scientific skills translate

| Scientific practice | Business analytics application |
|---|---|
| Define the observational unit and sampling frame | Specify the **grain** of each table and the unit of analysis. An order-line table can have many rows per order. Joining it to several support messages per order can multiply reported revenue. Reconcile totals before modeling. |
| Specify outcomes and measurement windows | Define the primary **KPI**, denominator, and time horizon. For a campaign, purchases per eligible recipient and purchases per email opener answer different questions. Track an adverse outcome, such as unsubscribes, as a guardrail. |
| Test a hypothesis against a comparison | Name the **incumbent**, the feasible alternative, and the decision owner. Match the evidence to the claim. Check temporal validation for forecasts and assignment or identification assumptions for treatment effects. |
| Quantify uncertainty and practical significance | Convert effects to business units such as contribution, cash flow, staff time, or service level. Show how uncertainty and different cost assumptions change the recommendation. |
| Make results reproducible | Record data definitions, cutoffs, code, and evidence versions. Report who acts on the result, whom it affects, how exceptions are handled, and when the decision is reviewed again. |

## Which analytical task answers the decision?

| Task | Example and evidence |
|---|---|
| **Measure** | Diagnose a conversion drop with verified counts, reporting windows, and comparable cohorts. |
| **Predict** | Estimate who is likely to leave. Check out-of-sample performance and calibration using information available at decision time. |
| **Estimate a causal effect** | Estimate who would stay **because of** an offer. Use randomized or credible quasi-experimental evidence and explain the identifying assumptions. |
| **Optimize** | Decide whom to contact under a campaign budget. Combine likely treatment effects with contribution, intervention costs, and constraints. Compare the resulting policy with the incumbent. |
| **Use generative AI** | Extract reasons from cancellation notes or draft support replies grounded in current policy. Evaluate whether claims follow from the evidence, measure cost and latency, and give the system an explicit way to abstain or hand off. |

See the [topic index](TOPIC_INDEX.md) for methods and the [business-function map](FIELD_MAP.md) for cases and datasets. The [working glossary](GLOSSARY.md) defines terms such as grain, estimand, and uplift.

## Worked example · From an effect estimate to a financial decision

A retailer sells one item per order at **$40**, with **$18** in landed product cost and **$6** in other variable costs. Each additional order contributes **$16**. A randomized email test estimates a **0.50 percentage-point** lift in the purchase rate. At the same effect across **10,000 eligible recipients**, that means 50 incremental orders. With a **$500** campaign cost, the estimated net contribution is **50 × $16 − $500 = $300**. The break-even lift is **$500 ÷ (10,000 × $16) = 0.3125 percentage points**.

If variable cost rises by $4 per order, net contribution falls to **$100** and break-even lift rises to about **0.42 percentage points**. If the estimated lift interval spans break-even, the financial conclusion is uncertain. Check whether the tested effect is likely to hold at scale, whether costs such as discounts and returns are included, and whether unsubscribes stay within the agreed limit. [Campaign decision lab](../labs/01_campaign_decision.ipynb)

## Evidence checklist

- What are the alternatives, who owns the decision, and what could they do differently?
- What are the data grain, eligible population, metric definition, and observation window?
- Does the evaluation show a descriptive pattern, predictive accuracy, a causal effect, or performance on a defined AI task?
- What are the relevant costs, benefits, constraints, and harms? How sensitive is the recommendation to assumptions?
- Who reviews exceptions and monitors real outcomes after deployment?

For current evidence about performance and deployment, see the [state-of-the-art summary](../resources/STATE_OF_THE_ART.md) and [research guide](../resources/RESEARCH.md).

documents.title: Working glossary
documents.markdown:
# Working glossary

Use these definitions to read business cases, interpret results, and find related methods in the [topic index](TOPIC_INDEX.md).

| Term | Working meaning |
|---|---|
| Business model | How the organization creates and delivers value, who pays, and what it costs to deliver. |
| Revenue | Sales recognized in the period, subject to the applicable accounting rules. Returns and discounts affect net sales. |
| Gross margin | Revenue less cost of goods sold. It may be expressed as money or as a fraction of revenue. |
| Contribution margin | Revenue less variable costs. It shows what remains to cover fixed costs and profit. Define which costs change for the decision under study. |
| Incremental value | Expected difference in value between a proposed action and the incumbent, after incremental costs. Write down the comparison and the time horizon. |
| Break-even | The level of performance where incremental benefits and costs are equal. Under constant unit margin, fixed cost divided by contribution per unit gives break-even volume. |
| Customer acquisition cost (CAC) | Acquisition spending divided by newly acquired customers for a specified cohort and period. Define how the spending numerator is attributed. |
| Customer lifetime value (CLV) | The expected value of future customer contribution over a stated horizon, often discounted. State whether acquisition and service costs are included. |
| Conversion rate | Eligible units that complete the defined event divided by all units in the stated denominator. Units might be customers, sessions, or assigned recipients. |
| Throughput | Units the process completes per unit of time, such as orders shipped per day. |
| Service level | A target for serving demand. Specify whether it refers to fill rate, probability of avoiding a stockout, or a time-to-service target. |
| Grain | What one row represents, such as one customer-day or one order line. Metric errors often start with mismatched grains. |
| Cohort | A group defined by a common starting event or period. Track cohorts on comparable time scales. |
| Incumbent / baseline | The current process or a simple reference method. For a pilot, choose the policy you could actually preserve if you reject the new one. |
| Data leakage | Information reaches training or evaluation that would be unavailable when the real decision is made. Future events and duplicated creatives can both leak. |
| Calibration | How well predicted probabilities align with observed frequencies on comparable cases. A well-calibrated group of 0.20 predictions has roughly 20% positives. |
| Forecast horizon | The distance between the time you make the forecast and the outcome you need to predict. Validate at the horizon the decision actually uses. |
| Estimand | The precise quantity you want to estimate. A campaign example is the seven-day purchase-rate difference under assignment to new copy versus current copy. |
| Intention-to-treat | The effect of being assigned to a treatment, comparing units according to original assignment. It preserves the random comparison when some recipients never open the email. |
| Absolute lift vs. relative lift | A rate rising from 5% to 6% gains 1 percentage point, or 20% relative to its original rate. Report the baseline and the unit. |
| Guardrail | A measure that can block launch even if the primary metric improves, such as an unsubscribe or false-approval limit. |
| Uplift | An estimated difference in outcomes under different interventions. A high propensity to purchase gives no direct estimate of whether an offer changes behavior. |
| Objective and constraints | The quantity the decision policy tries to maximize or minimize, and the limits it must respect. Forecast error and inventory cost are different objectives. |
| Embedding | A numerical representation learned from input such as text. Nearby vectors can indicate shared characteristics. Applicability still depends on the audience, offer, and context. |
| Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) | A system retrieves relevant evidence and supplies it to a generation model. Evaluate retrieval coverage, evidence applicability, and whether the model's claims follow from what it retrieved. |
| Agent | A system that selects steps or tools in pursuit of a goal. Define its permitted actions, evidence requirements, stop condition, and human handoff. |
| Evaluation set | A versioned collection of tasks and expected answers or decision criteria. Include ordinary cases, known failures, unusual inputs, and situations where the system should abstain. |
| Drift | A change in the data, task, or relationship between inputs and outcomes after deployment. Define what you monitor and how you respond. |

For foundational explanations and worked examples, see [SBA break-even guide](https://legacy.sba.gov/business-guide/plan-your-business/calculate-your-startup-costs/break-even-point), [OpenStax on marketing metrics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-marketing/pages/2-4-marketing-plan-progress-using-metrics), and the [book guide](../resources/BOOKS.md).

[Curriculum](https://business.ucdenver.edu/ms/business-analytics-and-artificial-intelligence) | Sequence prediction, causal evaluation, and generative AI around the same business outcome and data. |

[Curriculum](https://wpcarey.asu.edu/masters-programs/ai-business/academics) | Have teams map a workflow, run a comparison, estimate full cost, and propose staged approval. |

## A short class you could teach

**Can we prove the AI-written campaign created profitable lift?** Give students the campaign evidence and three draft recommendations, including one persuasive response with the wrong denominator. Have them estimate lift and uncertainty, incorporate the economics and unsubscribe threshold, then defend a recommendation. Change an assumption during the discussion and ask them what evidence would justify a different action.

Use a rubric that credits the estimand and baseline, traceable numbers, treatment of uncertainty, decision economics, and communication. Treat a recommendation that violates the guardrail as a decision error even if the calculations are correct. Compare [Eccles' public Marketing Text Analytics syllabus](https://class-tools.app.utah.edu/syllabus/1264/12473/MKTG%2B4640%2BSyllabus.pdf) with [BYU Marriott's Product Management course book](https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/) to see two different ways to teach application and evaluation.

## Find and evaluate evidence

- **Frame the question.** Write down the population and unit of analysis. For prediction, specify the horizon and validation split. For a causal claim, specify the intervention, comparator, estimand, and identification assumptions. For a decision, specify the objective, constraints, and cost of errors.
- **Match the source to the claim.** Use textbooks for methods, cases for operating context, and papers for empirical evidence. Browse [methods research](../resources/ANALYTICS_METHODS.md) for comparisons and [applied studies](../resources/BUSINESS_APPLICATIONS.md) for evidence about specific decisions. Read the design and setting before transferring an effect estimate. For agent benchmarks, inspect the task set, scoring rules, and failure modes.
- **Search the literature.** Combine a method with a use case, such as `"heterogeneous treatment effects" AND marketing` or `"forecasting" AND "inventory policy"`. Pair `"agent evaluation"` with a workflow or decision, then follow citations to compare related results. [Research worksheet](../resources/RESEARCH.md#a-reusable-reading-worksheet) · [Research trackers](../resources/ONLINE.md#follow-new-research)

# AI methods for business analytics

Reviewed November 18, 2026. These 15 peer-reviewed studies from 2025–2026 cover the workflows that turn business data into forecasts, estimates, and decisions. Read each result in light of its evaluation setting, such as a public benchmark, a historical backtest, a field experiment, or an enterprise deployment. Scite was used for discovery and bibliographic checks. Conference citations use the version in the official proceedings.

| If your question is… | Start with |
|---|---|
| Which customers, transactions, or orders are most likely to meet an outcome? | [Tabular prediction](#tabular-prediction) |
| What will demand be over the next planning window? | [Forecasting](#forecasting) |
| How much should we order, or which promotions should we run? | [Prescriptive analytics and optimization](#prescriptive-analytics-and-optimization) |
| What will change if we intervene, and for whom? | [Causal machine learning and experimentation](#causal-machine-learning-and-experimentation) |
| Can an assistant reproduce the right business metric? | [Analytics agents and text-to-SQL](#analytics-agents-and-text-to-sql) |

## Tabular prediction

- **Hollmann et al. (2025) — TabPFN.** This predictive benchmark shows what a pretrained model can do with a small labeled table. Use it when a new product, site, or customer segment has limited training data. Compare against a tuned tree model and a simpler baseline under the same labeling and compute constraints. [Nature](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08328-6)
- **Erickson et al. (2025) — TabArena.** This shared evaluation suite compares classical, neural, and foundation models across tabular tasks. Use the results to shortlist model families. Then evaluate probability calibration, cost, and runtime on an internal holdout by date or customer group. [NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks](https://doi.org/10.52202/085713-0519)
- **Qu et al. (2026) — TabICLv2.** The authors compare an open pretrained model for classification and regression against published baselines. The paper includes ablations and scale tests. Estimate the memory and latency at your intended scoring volume before treating a benchmark advantage as a deployment advantage. [ICML proceedings](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v306/qu26a.html)

**Practice.** For churn risk, compare logistic regression, gradient-boosted trees, and a tabular foundation model. Freeze the observation window before the churn label, tune on past cohorts, and report calibration and precision at the contact team's actual capacity. Use an experiment to estimate the effect of outreach.

## Forecasting

- **Qiao et al. (2026) — TIME benchmark.** This zero-shot evaluation uses 98 tasks across 50 datasets and is designed to reduce data leakage. Read how the authors match the available predictors and forecast horizon to the task. Follow the same procedure with store, product, and lead-time requirements. [ICML proceedings](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v306/qiao26g.html)
- **Muth, Engel, and Nufer (2026) — industrial orders.** This backtest compares pretrained and conventional methods for German industrial order forecasting across training histories of different lengths. Use its design to check which method works for short or sparse histories and whether its advantage survives at the required planning horizon. [Journal of Marketing Analytics](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1057/s41270-026-00489-9)
- **Zanotti (2025) — retail retraining schedules.** On two retail demand datasets, less frequent retraining maintained point and probabilistic forecasting accuracy while reducing compute cost. In your setting, compare refresh schedules over the same holdouts and test how each responds to assortment and demand changes. [Machine Learning with Applications](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mlwa.2025.100769)

**Practice.** Backtest a seasonal baseline, a global tree model, and a time-series foundation model at rolling forecast origins. Give each method the same information that would have been available at the decision date. Compare bias, quantile loss, and interval coverage, then carry the same forecasts into the [inventory decision lab](../labs/02_inventory_decision.py).

## Prescriptive analytics and optimization

- **An et al. (2025) — nonstationary demand.** This newsvendor study uses theory and backtests across three real datasets to evaluate how a policy can combine historical demand and current predictions. Use it to study what happens to ordering costs when demand shifts or forecast reliability changes. [Manufacturing & Service Operations Management](https://doi.org/10.1287/msom.2024.1168)
- **Jia, Schrotenboer, and Chen (2025) — inventory routing.** The model samples demand scenarios from predicted quantiles and passes them to a solver that coordinates deliveries and replenishment. Numerical experiments show how to compare decision policies under uncertainty. Check which routing, lead-time, and service constraints in the paper apply to your setting. [Transportation Science](https://doi.org/10.1287/trsc.2024.0613)
- **Llenas et al. (2026) — PepsiCo pricing and promotions.** This refereed deployment account explains how a planning team combines machine learning forecasts with mixed-integer optimization for promotions, and Bayesian elasticity models with nonlinear optimization for base prices. Read it for objectives, constraints, and workflow design. A causal estimate of the business gain requires its own comparison. [INFORMS Journal on Applied Analytics](https://doi.org/10.1287/inte.2025.0302) · [Open preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17941)

**Practice.** Hold the cost model and service target fixed. Compare an incumbent replenishment rule, a point-forecast rule, and a scenario-based policy on the same demand paths. Report total cost, stockouts, solver time, and the frequency of infeasible recommendations.

## Causal machine learning and experimentation

- **Ye et al. (2026) — combinations of treatments.** The authors use debiased deep learning to estimate responses to combinations of interventions. In three randomized experiments on a video-sharing platform, they used outcomes from tested combinations to check predictions made with only a subset of them. Inspect the structural assumptions before using a similar model to recommend an untested bundle. [Management Science](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.04625)
- **Sun et al. (2025) — context-aware uplift.** The authors benchmark an uplift model that uses both user and item context on synthetic and product data. Apply the design to an offer whose effect may vary with browsing context. Check overlap and evaluate incremental contribution after offer costs on untreated and treated holdout groups with known assignment probabilities. [KDD proceedings](https://doi.org/10.1145/3690624.3709293)
- **Ellickson et al. (2026) — new ad or offer text.** This study uses text representations and past promotion evidence to score candidate treatments. Its empirical validation includes held-out creatives. Read how the method assesses support for an unfamiliar proposal, then use a randomized challenger test for a rollout decision. [Journal of Marketing Research](https://doi.org/10.1177/00222437261476639)

**Practice.** In the [campaign tutorial](../labs/01_campaign_decision.ipynb), define the unit of randomization, outcome horizon, target population, and cost per contact. Compare an uplift-based targeting policy with a response-based policy and the incumbent. Estimate the value of each policy on held-out randomized records and quantify uncertainty.

## Analytics agents and text-to-SQL

- **Lei et al. (2025) — Spider 2.0.** This enterprise-style benchmark includes 632 workflow problems involving database metadata, long schemas, and SQL dialects. Use it to design realistic tasks that require inspecting joins, filters, time periods, and units. A benchmark score describes the evaluated tasks and configuration. [ICLR proceedings](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/46c10f6c8ea5aa6f267bcdabcb123f97-Abstract-Conference.html)
- **Chen et al. (2025) — adaptive abstention.** The authors evaluate an approach that can ask for help or abstain when uncertain about how to map a question to database fields. Use it to design tests for similarly named tables and ambiguous business terms. Measure answer coverage together with error rates among issued answers. [Proceedings of the ACM on Management of Data](https://doi.org/10.1145/3709719)
- **Ji et al. (2026) — enterprise retrieval and SQL.** BIRD-Ent and Spider-Ent test large schemas and scattered documents. The authors study retrieval of both schema and business knowledge before query generation. In a pilot, record whether the answer uses the correct metric definition and supporting sources as well as whether the query executes. [Findings of EMNLP](https://doi.org/10.18653/2026.findings-emnlp.1971)

**Practice.** Assemble read-only examples with known answers for common KPIs. Include conflicting metric definitions, time zones, nulls, and rows the requester should not access. Grade source choice, numeric correctness, scope, need for clarification, and reproduction of a result by another analyst. Use the [grounded Q&A lab](../labs/03_grounded_policy_qa.py) to practice scope and abstention.

## References

- An, L., Li, A. A., Moseley, B., & Ravi, R. (2025). The nonstationary newsvendor with (and without) predictions. *Manufacturing & Service Operations Management, 27*(3), 881–896. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1287/msom.2024.1168)
- Chen, K., Chen, Y., Koudas, N., & Yu, X. (2025). Reliable text-to-SQL with adaptive abstention. *Proceedings of the ACM on Management of Data, 3*(1), Article 69. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1145/3709719)
- Ellickson, P. B., Kar, W., Reeder, J. C., III, & Zeng, G. (2026). Evaluating novel unstructured treatments with generative AI: A causal prediction framework. *Journal of Marketing Research*. Advance online publication. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1177/00222437261476639)
- Erickson, N., Purucker, L., Tschalzev, A., Holzmüller, D., Desai, P., Salinas, D., & Hutter, F. (2025). TabArena: A living benchmark for machine learning on tabular data. *Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 38*. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.52202/085713-0519)

# Books for learning and teaching AI in business analytics

Verified November 18, 2026. Dates refer to the linked editions or drafts, dated 2023 onward. **Free** means the linked site offers the full text. **Commercial** means the publisher offers a purchase, subscription, or institutional access. Preview links are identified separately.

For a shortlist of books and courses released since January 2025, see [recent resources](RECENT_RESOURCES.md).

## Quick picks by use

- **Decision economics.** Start with chapter 5 of *Machine Learning for Business Analytics* and the churn case in Huntsinger's *Business Analytics*. Use the [campaign tutorial](../labs/01_campaign_decision.ipynb) to connect measured incremental lift, margin, and campaign cost.
- **Experimentation and causal inference.** Start with Dong's chapters on experimental design and randomized field experiments. For a causal ML extension, use the BERT and double machine learning notebook from *Applied Causal Inference Powered by ML and AI*.
- **Bayesian analysis.** Work through chapter 2 of Martin's *Bayesian Analysis with Python* on posterior-based decisions and predictive checks. Use Dong's marketing examples to practice updating beliefs when new customer data arrives.
- **AI workflow design and evaluation.** Read chapters 3 and 6 of *AI Engineering* and chapters 3, 5, and 8 of *Evals for AI Engineers*. Use the latter to add a failure taxonomy and regression tests to the AI analyst exercise.
- **Business-school survey.** Rezaee and colleagues survey applications, governance, and transformation. Sharda, Delen, and Turban provide a managerial analytics textbook, and Huntsinger provides decision cases.
- **Business audience.** *Strategic Analytics* connects quantitative methods to competition and managerial planning. Mollick's *Co-Intelligence* and *Co-Existence* offer practitioner perspectives on human–AI collaboration and how it may change work.

## Business decisions and graduate analytics

| Book | What to read and use | Edition and access |
|---|---|---|
| **Galit Shmueli, Peter C. Bruce, Peter Gedeck, and Nitin R. Patel, *Machine Learning for Business Analytics: Concepts, Techniques, and Applications in Python*** | Chapter 5 on classifier and ranking performance provides a starting point for comparing targeting models. Pair it with Huntsinger's churn case and have students defend a classification threshold using the cost of an offer and the expected value of retention. | Second Python edition, June 2025. Commercial, with contents and a first-chapter preview. [Wiley](https://www.wiley.com/en-us/machine-learning-for-business-analytics-concepts-techniques-and-applications-in-python-2nd-edition-p-9781394286805) |
| **Ramesh Sharda, Dursun Delen, and Efraim Turban, *Business Analytics, Data Science, and AI: A Managerial Approach*** | Chapter 6 for text, web, and social media analytics, chapter 8 for optimization and simulation, and chapters 10–11 for AI trends and managerial issues. A broad MSBA syllabus reference that connects descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive work. | Sixth edition, published 2026, copyright 2027. Commercial. [Pearson](https://www.pearson.com/en-us/subject-catalog/p/business-analytics-data-science-and-ai-a-managerial-approach/P200000013730/9780135437698) |
| **Zabihollah Rezaee, Joseph H. Zhang, Salem Lotfi Boumediene, and Nick J. Rezaee, *Business Analytics and Artificial Intelligence: Concepts, Skills and Real World Application*** | A broad survey that can orient technical readers to business uses. Chapters 6 and 8 cover strategy and prescriptive decisions. Chapters 12–14 cover industry applications, responsible use, and organizational transformation. For deeper work on experiments or agent evaluation, use the specialist sections below. This assessment is based on the publisher's contents and description. | First edition, released October 2026, copyright 2027. Commercial, with a publisher preview. [Routledge and contents](https://www.routledge.com/Business-Analytics-and-Artificial-Intelligence-Concepts-Skills-and-Real-World-Application/Rezaee-Zhang-Boumediene-Rezaee/p/book/9781041124009) |
| **Richard Huntsinger, *Business Analytics: Methods and Cases for Data-Driven Decisions*** | Use the telecom churn case in §6.4 to discuss retention and sensitivity analysis, then the call center scheduling case in §8.5 to connect predictions to resource decisions. The cases provide a model for teaching analytic methods through actual business decisions. | 2025. Commercial, with a free excerpt and detailed contents. [Cambridge](https://www.cambridge.org/highereducation/books/business-analytics/49F97FC7360294F70056ADDC895C61AE) · [Excerpt](https://assets.cambridge.org/97813165/12159/excerpt/9781316512159_excerpt.pdf) · [Contents](https://assets.cambridge.org/97813165/12159/frontmatter/9781316512159_frontmatter.pdf) |
| **Isaac Baley and Laura Veldkamp, *The Data Economy: Tools and Applications*** | Use the graduate economics treatment of data as a business input to ask when collecting, sharing, or purchasing additional information changes the value of a decision. Useful for discussing data strategy, welfare, and the economics of AI. | January 2025. Commercial. [Princeton University Press](https://press.princeton.edu/books/hardcover/9780691256726/the-data-economy) |

## Experiments and causal machine learning

| Book | What to read and use | Edition and access |
|---|---|---|
| **Xiaojing Dong, *Marketing Analytics and Data Science: Tools and Models*** | Read the chapters on Bayesian updating and experimental design and on causal analysis with a randomized field experiment. Apply them to a campaign experiment that defines the outcome, assignment unit, and decision threshold in advance. | First edition, May 2026. Commercial, with public chapter descriptions. [Palgrave Macmillan](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-032-11130-2) |
| **Victor Chernozhukov, Christian Hansen, Nathan Kallus, Martin Spindler, and Vasilis Syrgkanis, *Applied Causal Inference Powered by ML and AI*** | Chapter 5 covers identification with observed controls, chapter 10 includes the DoubleML notebook using BERT features, and chapters 14–15 cover heterogeneous effects and validation. Work through the notebooks before adapting the methods to customer or campaign data. | Author manuscript first released in 2024. Site updated September 25, 2026. Free text and Python/R notebooks. [Author site](https://causalml-book.org/) |
| **Matheus Facure, *Causal Inference in Python*** | Use the sections on evaluating conditional average treatment effects, cumulative gain, and decisions to compare targeting by predicted response with targeting by estimated incremental effect. | July 2023. Commercial, with public contents. [O’Reilly](https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/causal-inference-in/9781098140243/) |
| **Osvaldo Martin, *Bayesian Analysis with Python*** | Chapter 2 uses posterior distributions for decisions and predictive checks. Use PyMC and ArviZ to model uncertainty and compare the expected payoff of acting now with that of collecting more information. | Third edition, January 2024. Commercial book with free companion materials. [Packt](https://www.packtpub.com/en-us/product/bayesian-analysis-with-python-9781836644835) · [Author materials](https://bap.com.ar/) |

## Forecasting and operational decisions

| Book | What to read and use | Edition and access |
|---|---|---|
| **Rob J. Hyndman, George Athanasopoulos, Azul Garza, Cristian Challu, Max Mergenthaler, and Kin G. Olivares, *Forecasting: Principles and Practice, the Pythonic Way*** | Chapter 5 covers baselines, forecast intervals, and time-series cross-validation. Compare the chapter 8–9 statistical models with chapter 15's foundation models, then use chapter 11 to reconcile product and regional forecasts. | Python edition, 2026. Free online, updated October 31, 2026. [OTexts](https://otexts.com/fpppy/) · [Dated preface](https://otexts.com/fpppy/preface.html) |
| **Warren B. Powell, *Sequential Decision Analytics and Modeling: Modeling with Python*** | §§1.5 and 1.8 use inventory decisions to introduce uncertainty and policy evaluation. Chapter 3 applies the framework to adaptive market planning. Useful for teaching how repeated decisions should respond to new demand information. | Second edition, February 2026. Free author PDF, with Python materials. [Author site](https://warrenpowell.org/sdamodeling/) · [Book PDF](https://warrenpowell.org/assets/papers/sdam-2nd-edition.pdf) |

## Text intelligence and LLM development

| Book | What to read and use | Edition and access |
|---|---|---|
| **Daniel Jurafsky and James H. Martin, *Speech and Language Processing*** | Chapters 4–5 for classification baselines and embeddings. Chapter 7 for transformers and chapter 11 for information retrieval and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Eccles lists the draft in its Spring 2026 Marketing Text Analytics syllabus. | Third-edition author draft, August 19, 2026. Free. [Stanford book site](https://web.stanford.edu/~jurafsky/slp3/) · [Eccles syllabus](https://class-tools.app.utah.edu/syllabus/1264/12473/MKTG%2B4640%2BSyllabus.pdf) |
| **Chip Huyen, *AI Engineering*** | Chapters 3–4 cover evaluation methods and system design criteria, including correctness, cost, and latency. Chapter 6 covers retrieval, tool use, and agent failure modes. Use it as a design reference for an evidence-grounded analyst. | O’Reilly English edition, December 2024. Commercial. [O’Reilly](https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/ai-engineering/9781098166298/) |
| **Shreya Shankar and Hamel Husain, *Evals for AI Engineers*** | Start with chapter 3 on analyzing failed traces, then chapter 5 on automated evaluators and chapter 8 on evaluating tool calls and multistep agents. A focused reference for turning failures in an analytics workflow into regression cases. | October 2026. Commercial, with a free companion FAQ. [O’Reilly](https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/evals-for-ai/9798341660717/) · [Authors’ FAQ](https://hamel.dev/blog/posts/evals-faq/evals-faq.pdf) |

## Strategy, adoption, and governance

| Book | What to read and use | Edition and access |
|---|---|---|
| **Martin Kunc, *Strategic Analytics: Towards AI-based Strategy Planning*** | Use the strategy analytics chapter to connect descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analysis to competitive choices. Have students distinguish what the evidence shows from the assumptions that drive a proposed action. | Second edition, first published online January 2026. Commercial, with public contents. [Wiley](https://doi.org/10.1002/9781394316038) |
| **Ethan Mollick, *Co-Existence: The Next Phase of AI*** | Use Mollick's discussion of human–AI interaction to ask how teams should allocate work, decision authority, and oversight when AI can do more of a workflow. Treat the book's projections as propositions for class discussion and connect them to the [field evidence](RESEARCH.md#organizations-and-real-work). | October 2026. Commercial, with an open author companion site. [Portfolio](https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/813026/co-existence-by-ethan-mollick/) · [Author companion site](https://co-existence.ai/classic/) |
| **Ethan Mollick, *Co-Intelligence*** | This New York Times bestseller introduces working and learning with generative AI. Use it to discuss how people delegate tasks, retain judgment, and evaluate AI help. | April 2024. Commercial, with a publisher sample. [Portfolio](https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/741805/co-intelligence-by-ethan-mollick/) |
| **Thomas H. Davenport and Nitin Mittal, *All-In on AI: How Smart Companies Win Big with Artificial Intelligence*** | Use the company cases to discuss how established firms integrate analytics and AI into products and processes. Have students identify the operational capabilities that would need to be in place for a comparable rollout. | January 2023. Commercial, with a publisher preview. [Harvard Business Review Press](https://store.hbr.org/product/all-in-on-ai-how-smart-companies-win-big-with-artificial-intelligence/10599) |
| **Babak Hodjat and Antoine Blondeau, *The Agentic Enterprise*** | Chapter 4 for cost of ownership and ROI, chapter 6 for system design, and chapter 7 for responsibility and controls. Use the practitioner vignettes to compare rollout choices and to identify which claims would require measurement in your organization. | July 2026. Commercial. [O’Reilly](https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/the-agentic-enterprise/0642572274566/) |

# AI in business analytics by application

Use this guide to find recent peer-reviewed work on a decision your team or students can specify and measure. It includes predictive models used in operating decisions, generative AI used in workflows, and evaluations of how those systems are deployed. Scite and publisher records were checked November 18, 2026. Citation years follow journal issues when assigned.

[Marketing and customer research](#marketing-and-customer-research) · [Sales](#sales) · [Operations and supply chain](#operations-and-supply-chain) · [Finance, risk, and accounting](#finance-risk-and-accounting) · [Customer service](#customer-service) · [Product and people](#product-and-people)

## Marketing and customer research

- **Choose which creative to test.** In a WhatsApp field experiment with one e-commerce brand, users were randomized among AI-personalized video, personalized image, and generic video ads. The AI-personalized videos raised engagement by six to nine percentage points relative to the comparison groups. The test changes several aspects of the ads across the three groups. A follow-up that isolates AI production would hold format and personalization fixed and measure incremental purchases and contribution after creative costs. Kapoor, A., & Kumar, M. (2025). Frontiers: Generative AI and personalized video advertisements. *Marketing Science*, *44*(4), 733–747. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1287/mksc.2023.0494) · [Public MIT research brief](https://ide.mit.edu/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/RB-DRAFT__7-8-25.pdf)
- **Decide where to use AI in customer discovery.** A replication of qualitative and quantitative research with a food company compared human, model, and hybrid approaches. Expert judges favored the hybrid in the tasks studied, and examples and retrieved context improved some synthetic responses. Use the design to compare coding, theme generation, and hypothesis development on actual interview transcripts. Validate any claim about customer preferences against a separate human sample before changing a product or campaign. Arora, N., Chakraborty, I., & Nishimura, Y. (2025). AI–human hybrids for marketing research: Leveraging large language models (LLMs) as collaborators. *Journal of Marketing*, *89*(2), 43–70. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1177/00222429241276529)

Practice with incremental profit in the [campaign decision lab](../labs/01_campaign_decision.ipynb) and compare approaches to generalizing across creative in the [marketing research guide](RESEARCH.md#marketing-and-experimentation).

## Sales

- **Choose how to introduce an AI recommendation system.** A multinational pharmaceutical company tested the same system with different combinations of procedures, decision authority, training, and incentives. A difference-in-differences analysis estimated more client meetings when the design matched users' working styles and fewer meetings for the untailored design relative to the legacy system. The study also assessed units sold as a secondary measure. The authors caution about causal interpretation given the small number of clusters. A new pilot can randomize one change at a time or compare clearly defined bundles across enough comparable teams. Krakowski, S. M., Haftor, D., Luger, J., Pashkevich, N., & Raisch, S. (2026). Human-centered artificial intelligence: A field experiment. *Management Science*, *72*(1), 57–72. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2022.03849) · [Open Uppsala repository copy](https://uu.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2%3A1991857/FULLTEXT01.pdf)

## Operations and supply chain

- **Decide when planners may override a forecast.** A spare-parts retailer ran a field experiment that let merchants modify the forecasts feeding its inventory algorithm. Profitability was 4.92% higher on average with overrides than with automated forecasts alone in the studied setting. The evidence concerns the retailer's override policy and inputs. In another category, log override reasons and assess costs, stockouts, and profit on the affected items. Kesavan, S., Kushwaha, T., & Steele, D. (2026). Profit implications of judgmental adjustments to forecast inputs: Evidence from a large-scale field experiment. *Management Science*, *72*(1), 119–127. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.06321)
- **Allocate fulfillment capacity when demand surges.** Flipkart's implementation case describes a probabilistic forecaster and a stochastic optimizer that allocate capacity, with a separate rule that revises allocations as demand arrives. The case reports historical backtests, shadow comparisons, and tests of new policies. The platform changed multiple processes, so company-wide improvements cannot be assigned to the forecasting model alone. Use Figure 5 to trace the forecast through the capacity and service-level constraints. Agarwal, S., Agrawal, P., Allamsetty, A., Attavar, A., B, D., Bellala, G., Bhatnagar, S., Choudhari, H., Goel, V., Gupta, P., Kachroo, A., Kothadiya, J., KM, N., Kudupudi, S. A. K., Kumar, M., KVM, N., Modi, T., Moorthy, R., Nair, R. S., … Vyas, P. (2026). Faster, smarter, leaner: How Flipkart optimized its supply chain to unlock growth. *INFORMS Journal on Applied Analytics*, *56*(1), 42–57. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1287/inte.2025.0282)

The [inventory decision lab](../labs/02_inventory_decision.py) uses fictional demand to compare how models rank on forecast error and inventory cost.

## Finance, risk, and accounting

- **Audit the drivers of a credit model.** Using car-loan data, the authors apply a Shapley-based decomposition of AUC to identify input features that contribute to default ranking. Features that drive overall ranking gains can differ from features that explain individual predictions. Run a separate calibration and subgroup error analysis at thresholds used in the loan policy before drawing conclusions about how the policy affects applicants. Hué, S., Hurlin, C., Pérignon, C., & Saurin, S. (2026). Measuring the driving forces of predictive performance: Application to credit scoring. *Management Science*, *72*(11), 10156–10172. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2023.02025)
- **Check whether past earnings forecasts were truly out of sample.** Levy compares financial language models trained with different data cutoffs and tests arithmetic with and without tools. In the earnings task studied, apparent predictive performance can be explained by information from after the forecast date. Evaluate forecasts prospectively or use a model and inputs with auditable cutoffs. Recompute material numbers from source filings. Levy, B. (2026). Caution ahead: Numerical reasoning and look-ahead bias in AI models. *Journal of Accounting Research*, *64*(3), 1139–1188. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1111/1475-679X.70058)

For transaction classification and human review, see Choi and Xie's experiment in the [research guide](RESEARCH.md#organizations-and-real-work).

## Customer service

- **Decide when to show an agent suggested replies.** A meal-delivery company randomized customer-service agents' access to AI suggestions. Efficiency and customer sentiment improved for some conversations, including cancellations. In chats following a chatbot comprehension failure, subsequent assistance for the human agent could worsen sentiment. Review resolution, repeat contacts, and escalation separately for each reason the customer contacted support. Zhang, S., & Narayandas, D. (2026). Engaging customers with AI in online chats: Evidence from a randomized field experiment. *Management Science*, *72*(1), 73–95. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2022.03920)
- **Choose whether customers can bypass chatbot triage.** In incentivized online experiments, users chose chatbots less often than a model that minimizes expected service time predicted. The prospect of a transfer after an unsuccessful initial interaction contributed to that reluctance. Measure abandonment and time to resolution in your own queues before using a simulation to reallocate staff. Kagan, E., Dada, M., & Hathaway, B. (2026). Why are customers averse to service chatbots? *Manufacturing & Service Operations Management*, *28*(6), 1983–2003. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1287/msom.2024.1141)

Use the [grounded policy Q&A lab](../labs/03_grounded_policy_qa.py) to specify when a support system should answer, abstain, or escalate.

## Product and people

- **Decide where designers should use generation.** In controlled studies with students and professional designers, AI assistance improved creative work during ideation. During implementation it improved creativity for less experienced designers and reduced efficiency without a creativity gain for experts. Evaluate a specific product workflow by stage and include both idea quality and rework. Hou, J., Wang, L., Wang, G., Wang, H. J., & Yang, S. (2025). The double-edged roles of generative AI in the creative process: Experiments on design work. *Information Systems Research*. Advance online publication. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1287/isre.2024.0937)
- **Decide whether to expand access to a coding assistant.** Three randomized field experiments across companies exposed 4,867 software developers to different access conditions. The pooled estimate was a 26.08% increase in completed tasks associated with tool use, with a 10.3 percentage-point standard error and variation across the experiments. Evaluate delivered functionality, review and rework time, and defects alongside task counts before translating the result into capacity or hiring decisions. Cui, K. Z., Demirer, M., Jaffe, S., Musolff, L., Peng, S., & Salz, T. (2026). The effects of generative AI on high-skilled work: Evidence from three field experiments with software developers. *Management Science*, *72*(11), 9408–9420. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.00535)

## Compare two studies before applying either result

Write down the decision owner, eligible population, unit of assignment or observation, incumbent workflow, outcome window, and full costs. Compare studies that answer the same decision question with different data or approaches. For example, compare a retailer's randomized override experiment with Flipkart's deployment case. The first estimates the value of allowing overrides in that setting. The second shows how forecasting and optimization connect to capacity limits and operating controls.

Use the [research worksheet](RESEARCH.md#a-reusable-reading-worksheet) to record the comparison or the [field map](../learning/FIELD_MAP.md) to find cases and exercises for a different function.

# Courses for learning and teaching AI in business analytics

Selected for applied work, quality of public materials, and fit with a learner who already knows machine learning and causal inference. Listings refer to a course release or offering from 2023 onward. Access and published prices were checked on November 18, 2026. **Open materials** means the linked notes, syllabi, or assignments are public. **Free course** means the provider offers instruction without a fee.

See [recent resources](RECENT_RESOURCES.md) for selected course materials released since January 2025.

## Quick picks by topic

- **Marketing analytics and text intelligence.** Use Eccles MKTG 4640 as a classroom model. Complete its review-analysis project with a simple baseline and a modern model from the Hugging Face course. Compare errors before recommending a service or marketing change.
- **AI workflows and evaluation.** Read BYU Marriott's “Models in Your Product,” then work through Stanford CS329Z's November 4 and 11 evaluation lectures. Build a small test set with correct, ambiguous, and unsupported business requests.
- **Evidence for adoption.** Read Columbia's Business Experiments syllabus for an MBA teaching model. Continue with Stanford's advanced treatment-effect and policy-learning draft when the rollout question varies by segment.
- **Bayesian modeling.** Use Richard McElreath's 2026 lecture on multilevel models to compare partial pooling with separate estimates for each store, product, or customer segment.

## Business analytics and marketing

| Course | Use it for | Access and source |
|---|---|---|
| **University of Utah Eccles · Marketing Text Analytics (MKTG 4640)** | See how a business school teaches unstructured text as evidence. The Yelp restaurant project on pages 8–10 asks learners to use sentiment, topics, and segmentation to make recommendations about service, menus, and promotions. | **Open syllabus and project brief**, Spring 2026. [Official syllabus and project](https://class-tools.app.utah.edu/syllabus/1264/12473/MKTG%2B4640%2BSyllabus.pdf#page=8) |
| **Columbia Business School · Business Analytics (B8101)** | Review how an MSBA course connects machine learning and business cases with A/B testing, causal inference, ethics, and optimization. Use the outline to design a case that asks students to predict an outcome, test an intervention, and choose a policy. | **Public course description**, Fall 2026. Campus enrollment is limited to MSBA students. [Columbia catalog](https://courses.business.columbia.edu/B8101) |

## Finance and risk

| Course | Use it for | Access and source |
|---|---|---|
| **University of Southampton · Artificial Intelligence in Finance (MANG6605)** | See how a graduate finance module teaches Python-based forecasting, document analysis, portfolio and risk modeling, and generative AI. Use its project format to require a reproducible analysis, a business justification, and a discussion of model risk. | **Public syllabus and assessment outline**, 2026–27. [Southampton module](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2026-27/modules/mang6605) |

## Experimentation and causal decision-making

| Course | Use it for | Access and source |
|---|---|---|
| **Columbia Business School · Business Experiments: Analytics for Causal Insight (B8257)** | Use the MBA syllabus as a model for teaching experimental design, implementation, and analysis around decisions managers face. Draft a primary evaluation metric, assignment unit, and decision rule for an AI rollout. | **Open catalog and section syllabi**, Fall 2026. [Columbia catalog](https://courses.business.columbia.edu/B8257) |

Use the syllabus to see how estimands and assumptions fit a manager's decision. The current program catalog describes Causal Analytics I and II. | **Open syllabus**, Fall 2025. [Historical syllabus](https://class-tools.app.utah.edu/syllabus/1258/17063/Syllabus%2Bfor%2BMKTG%2B6600-001%2BFall%2B2025%2BBus%2BDecision%2BAlgorithm.pdf) · [Current Eccles MSBA curriculum](https://eccles.utah.edu/programs/master-of-science-in-business-analytics/academics/) |

Rework a multilevel example to estimate demand or conversion across business segments with different sample sizes. | **Open 2026 recordings, code, and exercises**. [Instructor's course materials](https://github.com/rmcelreath/stat_rethinking_2026#calendar--topical-outline) |

Its discount-code example connects experimental design to a rollout decision. | **Paid cohort course**, offered November 2026. Public syllabus.
