documents.title: Datasets and benchmarks for business analytics
documents.markdown:
# Datasets and benchmarks for business analytics

Choose an exercise by the decision and the kind of evidence the data can support. Record the dataset version or release quarter when you download it. Publisher pages and access notes checked November 18, 2026.

| If you want to practice… | Start with |
|---|---|
| Sales measurement and customer text analysis | [Sales and customer analytics](#sales-and-customer-analytics) |
| Estimating the effect of AI access or planning media spend | [Experiments and marketing decisions](#experiments-and-marketing-decisions) |
| Forecasting demand and deciding how much to stock | [Demand and inventory](#demand-and-inventory) |
| Checking financial numbers and evidence | [Finance and accounting](#finance-and-accounting) |
| Evaluating an analytics agent | [SQL and analytics agents](#sql-and-analytics-agents) |
| Measuring AI use across firms and industries | [Business adoption](#business-adoption) |

## Sales and customer analytics

| Resource | Exercise | Interpretation and access |
|---|---|---|
| **Maven Sales Challenge, April 2024.** Fictional B2B CRM data with linked accounts, opportunities, products, and sales teams. | Reconcile won revenue by quarter and build a win-rate scorecard. State how you count opportunities open at the end of a quarter. | The records describe a fictional business. Check which fields were available at the scoring date before using them as predictors. The challenge links the sample. [Dataset and brief](https://mavenanalytics.io/challenges/maven-sales-challenge) |
| **CFPB Consumer Complaint Database, select a 2023–2026 extract.** Public complaints about financial products, with narratives where consumers provided consent and publication rules were met. | Label a small set of narratives for routing and compare a text baseline with an LLM. Audit errors where the wrong team would delay resolution. | Use a dated extract. Report missing narratives and review the publisher’s coverage notes before comparing firms or products. [Data, download options, and coverage](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/data-research/consumer-complaints/) |
| **Microsoft Fabric churn tutorial, 2026 documentation.** Worked example covering ingestion, exploration, modeling, and Power BI reporting. | Trace a churn prediction from raw data to a report. Check when inputs were available and independently verify the totals that appear in the dashboard. | The tutorial uses a bank customer dataset. A Fabric workspace is required for the full workflow. A churn prediction alone does not estimate the effect of a retention offer. [Tutorial and data instructions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/data-science/tutorial-data-science-introduction) |

## Experiments and marketing decisions

| Resource | Exercise | Interpretation and access |
|---|---|---|
| **Noy and Zhang’s professional writing experiment, 2023.** Public study materials and an author-linked replication package. | Reproduce a comparison of elapsed time or assessed quality by assignment. Record the assignment rule and choose one outcome before fitting subgroup models. | The randomized comparison concerns selected professional writing tasks. Use the data and code link in the author supplement. [Author supplement](https://shakkednoy.com/Noy%20Zhang%20NBER%20SI.pdf#page=11) · [*Science* article](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adh2586) |
| **Google Meridian sample notebooks, open-source release in 2025.** Example data and code for marketing mix modeling and budget allocation. | Compare two allocations after changing a channel ROI prior or the calibration evidence. Record how much the decision moves. | The notebook demonstrates the model and its assumptions. In a live deployment, validate recommendations against intervention evidence where possible. [Notebook catalog](https://developers.google.com/meridian/notebook) |
| **Campaign decision lab.** Repository-generated fictional data for a randomized promotion. | Estimate incremental purchases and contribution, then test whether targeting based on estimated incremental response improves the decision. | The data generator is visible, which makes the exercise reproducible and lets learners check the gap between known and estimated lift. [Notebook](../labs/01_campaign_decision.ipynb) |

## Demand and inventory

| Resource | Exercise | Interpretation and access |
|---|---|---|
| **FreshRetailNet-50K, May 2025.** Dingdong’s 50,000 store–product series include hourly sales, stockout indicators, and contextual variables. | Compare a seasonal baseline with a candidate model. Evaluate on later dates, analyze performance by stockout exposure, and compare resulting inventory decisions under specified overage and shortage costs. | A stockout limits observed sales. Demand that went unserved must be estimated. Hold origins and information constant across methods. CC BY 4.0. [Data card](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Dingdong-Inc/FreshRetailNet-50K) · [Baseline code](https://github.com/Dingdong-Inc/frn-50k-baseline) · [Wang et al., 2025 preprint](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2505.16319) |
| **GIFT-Eval, October 2024.** General time-series benchmark with datasets and standard evaluation code. | Compare the same forecasts at multiple horizons with a seasonal baseline. Use the official splits and review each candidate model’s training sources. | Aggregate scores combine heterogeneous series. Inspect performance on series relevant to the intended decision before transferring a ranking. Check the terms of individual datasets. [Data and evaluation code](https://github.com/SalesforceAIResearch/gift-eval) · [Aksu et al., 2024 preprint](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2410.10393) |

## Finance and accounting

| Resource | Exercise | Interpretation and access |
|---|---|---|
| **SEC Financial Statement Data Sets, 2026 quarterly releases.** Public structured data extracted from filings. | Pick a company and compare revenue, operating income, and cash flow across periods. Reconcile discrepancies with the source filing and record the units, period, form, and accession identifier. | Keep track of amendments, duplicate contexts, and filing versus fiscal dates. The SEC provides downloads and documentation for the tables. [Quarterly data and documentation](https://www.sec.gov/dera/data/financial-statement-data-sets.html) |
| **FinanceBench, 2023.** Annotated financial questions grounded in public company documents. | Compare retrieval plus calculation against an answer-only baseline. Score the selected company, period, units, calculation, and cited evidence. | The public sample has 150 examples. The full collection has separate access arrangements. Check the dataset terms and use new questions from later filings when measuring generalization. [Public sample and source documents](https://github.com/patronus-ai/financebench) · [Islam et al., 2023 preprint](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2311.11944) |

## SQL and analytics agents

| Resource | Exercise | Interpretation and access |
|---|---|---|
| **Spider 2.0, ICLR 2025.** Multi-step text-to-SQL tasks derived from enterprise data workflows. | Compare a model’s generated answer with SQL that a human independently checked. Grade the returned rows, metric definition, and query grain. Start with the SQLite tasks in the Lite setting for local practice. | Record the task version and database engine. Check author access notes for hosted warehouses. A benchmark pass measures task performance under that setup. [Task variants and access](https://spider2-sql.github.io/) · [Code and update log](https://github.com/xlang-ai/Spider2) · [Lei et al., ICLR 2025](ANALYTICS_METHODS.md#references) |
| **DataSpace, August 2026.** Benchmark for data agents working across heterogeneous artifacts. | Evaluate whether a model returns a complete, verifiable table. Inspect a wrong answer to see whether retrieval, joining, or interpretation caused the error. | Start with paper examples to design verifiable tasks on data you can inspect. The benchmark and scoring protocol are described in the preprint. [Li et al., 2026 preprint](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2608.03451) |

## Business adoption

| Resource | Exercise | Interpretation and access |
|---|---|---|
| **U.S. Census Business Trends and Outlook Survey (BTOS), 2026 AI supplement.** Public survey estimates on use across firms, functions, and tasks. | Compare adoption rates across sectors or size categories. Report the question wording, survey period, population, uncertainty, and whether estimates are firm- or employment-weighted. | The core AI questions changed in November 2025, and Census started a new series with the December 4 release. Compare like definitions. Reported adoption does not estimate an effect on firm performance. [Downloads](https://www.census.gov/hfp/btos/data_downloads?so=1) · [Question wording update](https://www.census.gov/hfp/btos/downloads/AI%20Question%20Wording%20Updates.pdf) · [Bonney et al., October 2026 working paper revision](https://www2.census.gov/ces/wp/2026/CES-WP-26-25R.pdf) |

## Benchmark and survey citations

- Aksu, T., Woo, G., Liu, J., Liu, X., Liu, C., Savarese, S., Xiong, C., & Sahoo, D. (2024). GIFT-Eval: A benchmark for general time series forecasting model evaluation. arXiv preprint. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2410.10393)
- Bonney, K., Breaux, C., Dinlersoz, E., Foster, L., Haltiwanger, J., & Pande, A. (2026). The microstructure of AI diffusion: Evidence from firms, business functions, and worker tasks. U.S. Census Bureau Center for Economic Studies, Working Paper CES 26-25R. [October revision](https://www2.census.gov/ces/wp/2026/CES-WP-26-25R.pdf)
- Islam, P., Kannappan, A., Kiela, D., Qian, R., Scherrer, N., & Vidgen, B. (2023). FinanceBench: A new benchmark for financial question answering. arXiv preprint. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2311.11944)
- Wang, Y., Gu, J., Long, L., Li, X., Shen, L., Fu, Z., Zhou, X., & Jiang, X. (2025). FreshRetailNet-50K: A stockout-annotated censored demand dataset for latent demand recovery and forecasting in fresh retail. arXiv preprint. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2505.16319)

See the [methods bibliography](ANALYTICS_METHODS.md#references) for Spider 2.0 and the [research bibliography](REFERENCES.md) for Noy and Zhang and DataSpace.

## Document the analysis

Record the **version, unit, and eligible rows**, including filters and exclusions. Define the **decision, baseline, and test set** before trying more models. Link the raw inputs, show how metrics reconcile, and report performance alongside the **cost of errors or change in the operating outcome**. For an experiment, include assignment and uncertainty. For generated answers, keep enough evidence for a reviewer to reproduce the result.

[Online resources](ONLINE.md) · [Runnable labs](../labs/README.md)

documents.title: Influential theories and frameworks
documents.markdown:
# Influential theories and frameworks

Some ideas explain how firms or people behave. Others specify an estimand, derive a decision rule, describe an empirical pattern, or guide implementation. The readings show how these ideas are taught or applied in sources published or updated since 2023.

## Framing and identifying the problem

| Idea and type | Business use | Scope or limitation | Recent reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CRISP-DM** · project methodology | Translate a business goal into an analytical question, then iterate through data understanding, preparation, modeling, evaluation, and deployment. Use it to assign deliverables and decide when an evaluation should send the team back to data preparation. | Teams still need to specify the causal design, production monitoring, and safeguards appropriate to the project. | [IBM, *CRISP-DM in SPSS Modeler*, version 19 documentation (2025)](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/spss-modeler/19.0.0?topic=overview-crisp-dm-in-spss-modeler) |
| **Explanation versus prediction** · statistical distinction | Choose the evaluation for the goal. A demand forecast needs an honest future holdout. A claim that a price change caused the demand shift needs an identification strategy. | Predictive performance establishes how well a model predicts under the conditions of the test. A causal explanation depends on assumptions about the data-generating process. | [Chernozhukov et al., *Applied Causal Inference Powered by ML and AI*, first two parts (2026 online update)](https://causalml-book.org/) |
| **Potential outcomes** · causal inference framework | Define effects by comparing outcomes under specified alternative actions for a population. An experiment can estimate average incremental purchases attributable to an offer. | For a given unit, only the outcome under the action taken is observed. Observational estimates depend on identifying assumptions such as exchangeability and overlap. | [Wager, *Causal Inference: A Statistical Learning Approach*, chapters 1–2 (2026 draft)](https://web.stanford.edu/~swager/causal_inf_book.pdf) |
| **Online controlled experiments** · experimental practice | Randomly assign eligible units, define outcomes and guardrails, and compare a new offer or workflow with the incumbent. Use a holdout or control to estimate the effect of assignment. | Interference, missing outcomes, invalid instrumentation, and repeated looks can undermine interpretation. Effects refer to the tested population, units, and time window. | [Larsen et al., *Statistical Challenges in Online Controlled Experiments* (2024 issue)](https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.2023.2257237) · [Chou et al., *From More to Better* (2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16335) |
| **Heterogeneous effects and uplift** · causal modeling and targeting | Estimate how treatment effects vary with pre-treatment attributes. Causal forests are one method. In customer retention, compare a policy that targets estimated incremental response with an incumbent targeting rule. | Subgroup effect estimates can be noisy, and the original design still determines whether the effects are identified. Evaluate the resulting policy on separate data with costs and constraints. | [Wager, *Causal Inference: A Statistical Learning Approach*, chapters 4–5 (2026 draft)](https://web.stanford.edu/~swager/causal_inf_book.pdf) |

## Turning estimates into decisions

| Idea and type | Business use | Scope or limitation | Recent reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Value of information** · decision theory | Estimate the improvement in expected value when a decision can use new information. Compare the benefit of buying data or running a pilot with its cost and the value lost while waiting. | The estimate depends on the available actions, outcome probabilities, consequences, and assumptions about how the evidence will influence action. | [Sadatsafavi et al., *Expected Value of Sample Information Calculations for Risk Prediction Model Validation* (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1177/0272989X251314010) |
| **Predictive to prescriptive analytics** · optimization framework | Use features and predicted uncertainty to choose an action under a business objective and constraints. For staffing, evaluate the schedule it produces using labor cost and service performance. | The objective needs to reflect relevant consequences. Test decisions under realistic constraints and changes in demand. | [Powell, *Sequential Decision Analytics and Modeling*, 2nd ed. (2026)](https://warrenpowell.org/sdamodeling/) · [Bertsimas, Everest, and Stoumpou, *Multimodal Prescriptive Deep Learning* (2026)](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=AwfWOCVLbJ) |
| **Newsvendor problem** · single-period inventory model | Choose an order quantity from the demand distribution by balancing shortage and overage costs. Under the standard linear cost model, the target demand quantile is shortage cost divided by the sum of shortage and overage costs. | The basic rule applies to a single period with the specified cost model. Replenishment during the period, shared capacity, or multi-period carryover changes the decision problem. | [Kocabıyıkoğlu et al., *Newsvendor Decisions Under Incomplete Information* (2024)](https://academic.oup.com/imaman/article/35/3/427/7642690) |

## Work, adoption, and governance

| Idea and type | Business use | Scope or limitation | Recent reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sociotechnical systems** · work-design theory | Study tools, roles, incentives, and coordination together. When adding AI to support work, examine who verifies drafts, handles exceptions, and bears additional review work. | The analysis depends on the actual work setting. Observe how the team adapts after deployment and measure both output quality and workload. | [Stanford Digital Economy Lab, *The Enterprise AI Playbook* (2026 deployment cases)](https://digitaleconomy.stanford.edu/publication/enterprise-ai-playbook/) |
| **Technology acceptance model** · information-systems theory | Use perceived usefulness and ease of use to formulate adoption hypotheses. Measure those perceptions alongside sustained usage for a new analytics tool. | Adoption intent, sustained use, and business value require separate measures. Access requirements, incentives, and implementation can affect each one. | [Nguyen et al., *Navigating Workplace AI Adoption* (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1017/jmo.2026.10090) |
| **Dynamic capabilities** · strategy theory | Examine how a firm senses opportunities, commits resources, and reconfigures routines. An AI pilot that works in one team may demand reusable data, oversight, and staff skills before it can scale. | Specify which capabilities are observable and what outcomes would show improvement. Changes in performance require separate evidence. | [Wong and Ngai, *Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Operational Performance: The Role of Dynamic Capabilities* (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.im.2025.104162) |
| **Task-based economics of automation** · economic framework | Describe work as a bundle of tasks. Identify which tasks technology performs, where people remain complementary, and which new tasks emerge, such as verification or evaluation. | A task-level productivity gain is one input into labor and organizational outcomes. Demand, reassignment, and newly created tasks also matter. | [Acemoglu, *The Simple Macroeconomics of AI* (2025 issue)](https://doi.org/10.1093/epolic/eiae042) |
| **Jagged technological frontier** · empirical finding and interpretive lens | Evaluate AI assistance at the task level. The field experiment found that consultants performed better on a set of tasks within the tested model's capabilities, and worse on a task selected outside them. | Where the boundary falls depends on the model, tools, users, and task. Test the actual workflow and its consequential failure cases. | [Dell’Acqua et al., *Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier* (2026 journal article)](https://doi.org/10.1287/orsc.2025.21838) |
| **NIST AI Risk Management Framework** · voluntary governance framework | Use Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage to assign owners, identify impacts, evaluate risks, and plan responses. Apply the generative AI profile to decisions about evidence, monitoring, and incidents. | The organization still has to define acceptable thresholds and demonstrate that its controls work in the use case. | [NIST AI RMF 1.0 (2023)](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/AI/NIST.AI.100-1.pdf) · [Generative AI Profile (2024)](https://www.nist.gov/publications/artificial-intelligence-risk-management-framework-generative-artificial-intelligence) |

See the [field primer](../learning/FIELD_PRIMER.md) for a worked translation from evidence into business value, the [topic index](../learning/TOPIC_INDEX.md) for technical resources, and the [state-of-the-art summary](STATE_OF_THE_ART.md) for current research and practice.

documents.title: Journals for AI in business analytics
documents.markdown:
# Journals for AI in business analytics

Choose a venue by the claim you want to investigate. **Management Science, Information Systems Research, and MIS Quarterly** are useful anchors for business decisions, digital systems, and organizational outcomes. Use the specialty journals to find work with the relevant setting and methods. This guide prioritizes fit to the research question.

[Research papers](RESEARCH.md) · [State of the art](STATE_OF_THE_ART.md) · [Researchers and labs](PEOPLE.md) · [Topic index](../learning/TOPIC_INDEX.md)

## Core business and information systems

| Journal | What to look for | Audience and typical evidence |
|---|---|---|
| [Management Science](https://pubsonline.informs.org/journal/mnsc) | Business effects of AI, firm and platform decisions, pricing, and analytics methods with practical consequences | Management and analytics scholars. Field experiments, empirical analysis, analytical models, and optimization. |
| [Information Systems Research](https://pubsonline.informs.org/journal/isre) | AI and digital platforms, economic value of information systems, and building and evaluating technology in organizations | Information systems and digital business researchers. Empirical, design, theoretical, and analytical work. [Editorial scope](https://pubsonline.informs.org/page/isre/editorial-statement) |
| [MIS Quarterly](https://aisel.aisnet.org/misq/) | Technology adoption, responsible design, governance, digital work, and organizational or societal effects | Information systems scholars. Research that develops theory or evaluates technology across users, firms, or institutions. |

## Marketing and customer analytics

| Journal | What to look for | Audience and typical evidence |
|---|---|---|
| [Marketing Science](https://pubsonline.informs.org/journal/mksc) | Ad incrementality, customer response, targeting, marketplaces, demand estimation, and pricing | Quantitative marketing researchers. Econometric and structural models, experiments, and analytical work. |
| [Journal of Marketing Research](https://www.ama.org/journal-of-marketing-research/) | Marketing measurement, customer behavior, how creative affects response, and empirical designs for marketing decisions | Marketing researchers across quantitative and behavioral methods. Experiments, observational studies, and measurement methods. |

## Operations, forecasting, and applied analytics

| Journal | What to look for | Audience and typical evidence |
|---|---|---|
| [Operations Research](https://pubsonline.informs.org/journal/opre) | Optimization, stochastic models, queues, and decisions under uncertainty | Operations research and decision science researchers. Mathematical models, proofs, algorithms, and computational evaluation. |
| [Manufacturing & Service Operations Management](https://pubsonline.informs.org/journal/msom) | Inventory, supply chains, service capacity, fulfillment, and prediction linked to operating decisions | Operations management scholars. Analytical, empirical, and computational work tied to operating processes. |
| [International Journal of Forecasting](https://forecasters.org/ijf/) | Probabilistic forecasts, forecast competitions, retail demand, forecast evaluation, and implementation | Forecasting researchers and practitioners. Compare forecasts at the relevant horizon and inspect the validation design and error measures. |
| [Journal of Business Analytics](https://www.tandfonline.com/jba) | Applied modeling methods and case studies with real-world data | Business analytics researchers and practitioners. Look for reproducible comparisons and how the study connects outputs to a decision. |

## Strategy, organizations, economics, and accounting

| Journal | What to look for | Audience and typical evidence |
|---|---|---|
| [Organization Science](https://pubsonline.informs.org/journal/orsc) | Human–AI teamwork, expertise, work design, coordination, and organizational learning | Organization researchers. Field experiments, observational and qualitative studies, and theory. |
| [Strategic Management Journal](https://sms.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/hub/journal/10970266/homepage/productinformation.html) | AI and firm capabilities, organizational adaptation, resource allocation, and competitive advantage | Strategy researchers. Empirical, qualitative, computational, and theoretical studies of firm decisions and outcomes. |
| [The Quarterly Journal of Economics](https://academic.oup.com/qje/pages/About) | Productivity, labor, technology adoption, and economic mechanisms behind observed effects | Economists. Look for credible identification, the setting and comparison group, and who experiences the effects. |
| [Journal of Accounting Research](https://www.chicagobooth.edu/research/chookaszian/journal-of-accounting-research) | AI-assisted accounting work, disclosure, controls, and audit or financial-information quality | Accounting researchers. Archival, experimental, and analytical approaches to how financial information is created and used. |

## Statistical and machine learning methods

| Journal | What to look for | Audience and typical evidence |
|---|---|---|
| [The Econometrics Journal](https://academic.oup.com/ectj/pages/About) | Causal machine learning, estimation, inference, and what changes when assumptions fail | Applied econometricians and methodologists. Theory, simulations, and applications with attention to identification and inference. |
| [Journal of Machine Learning Research](https://www.jmlr.org/) | Modeling methods, evaluation protocols, benchmark design, and reproducibility | Machine learning researchers. Read the experimental setup and assess how the data, baselines, and tasks relate to your business setting. Journal articles are openly accessible. |

## Other publication types

| Source | What it helps you find | How to use it |
|---|---|---|
| Working paper servers and preprint archives | Early results, public methods, and replication files. [NBER Working Papers](https://www.nber.org/papers) · [arXiv Artificial Intelligence](https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/recent) | Record the version and review status. Search the exact title and authors for a published version, then compare the methods and findings. |
| Conference and workshop proceedings | Technical advances and emerging benchmarks, often before journal articles. [Proceedings of Machine Learning Research](https://proceedings.mlr.press/) | Name the venue and track. Check the review process, dataset, baselines, and whether the setting supports the claim you are making. |
| Practitioner outlets | Management questions, implementation patterns, and links to case studies or research. [Harvard Business Review](https://hbr.org/topic/subject/ai-and-machine-learning) · [Knowledge at Wharton](https://knowledge.wharton.upenn.edu/ai-in-focus-series/) | Use practical accounts to frame a problem. For an empirical claim, trace the cited study and check the design and uncertainty. |

**Compare across venues.** For human–AI work, pair *Generative AI at Work* in *QJE* with *Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier* in *Organization Science*. For each one, record the task, who was studied, how AI access was assigned or introduced, the outcome, and where the effect varied. For marketing, compare *Generative Artificial Intelligence and Sales Productivity* in *Management Science* with *Evaluating Novel Unstructured Treatments with Generative AI* in *JMR*. The [paper guide](RESEARCH.md) links all four and summarizes their evidence.

Venue and scope links checked November 18, 2026. Full-text access varies by article and institution.

# Online resources for AI in business analytics

Reviewed November 18, 2026. Browse public business-school cases, datasets, practical guidance, and research feeds. The Wharton–Petco case and the writing experiment materials complement the [campaign tutorial](../labs/01_campaign_decision.ipynb).

For a date-filtered shortlist, see [recent resources](RECENT_RESOURCES.md).

## How businesses and business schools use AI

1. **Wharton–Petco email marketing case.** This public student-project write-up is the closest match to the tutorial. The team extracted text and image features, predicted click-through rates, and retrieved historical creative to generate new emails. Sketch the same workflow and specify the randomized comparison you would need to measure incremental purchases. The write-up describes the project and its reported impact. [Wharton case](https://ai-analytics.wharton.upenn.edu/student-programs/analytics-accelerator/optimizing-petcos-email-marketing-strategy-using-generative-ai/)
2. **MIT Sloan, The Cemex Journey to AI at Scale.** A real order-to-fulfillment case for teaching how data foundations, model monitoring, and business ownership keep AI working across markets. Identify who should approve the model, own the metric, and respond to drift. MIT's 2026 teaching page links to the open 2024 working paper. [Teaching objectives](https://mitsloan.mit.edu/teaching-resources-library/cemex-journey-to-ai-scale) · [Full case](https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/175416)
3. **INSEAD, Taming GenAI to Automate Business Processes.** The publisher lists this as a free case. Use it to compare predictive AI, generative AI, rules, and human review within the same process. As a discussion exercise, mark which steps to automate and which decisions require a person. [Aloma case](https://publishing.insead.edu/case/taming-genai-automate-business-processes-aloma-example)
4. **Wharton AI & Analytics Accelerator.** The Fall 2026 briefs show what a business-school capstone is expected to deliver. Expedia's brief is on evaluating a multimodal travel agent, and RxSense's is on forecasting returns to enterprise AI investment. For one brief, draft a one-page plan with the decision owner, data requirements, a baseline, and success criteria. The briefs are public. The program works with sponsor data under its own access arrangements. [Current project briefs and past cases](https://ai-analytics.wharton.upenn.edu/for-students/ai-analytics-accelerator/)
5. **Eccles Marketing Text Analytics.** The Spring 2026 syllabus pairs text analysis, primarily in R, with a Yelp restaurant review project. Its project brief shows how students move from sentiment and topics to recommendations on service, menus, or promotions. Use it to design a short exercise that asks students to justify a business decision from text evidence. [Eccles syllabus and project brief](https://class-tools.app.utah.edu/syllabus/1264/12473/MKTG%2B4640%2BSyllabus.pdf#page=8)

## Datasets and notebooks for practice

Use [datasets and benchmarks](DATASETS.md) to find data by decision. The guide links to experiments, CRM records, financial statements, retail stockout data, SQL benchmark tasks, and AI adoption estimates. Each entry gives an exercise and explains what conclusions the data can support.

## Test AI workflows and analytics decisions

6. **Statistical Challenges in Online Controlled Experiments (2024 issue).** Use the peer-reviewed methods review to identify pitfalls in randomization, repeated testing, and metric design before analyzing the campaign lab. [A/B testing methodology review](https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.2023.2257237)
7. **Anthropic, Demystifying Evals for AI Agents.** An engineering guide to scoring the result and inspecting the trace. Start with a few known failure cases, such as a wrong denominator, an unauthorized action, and a missing cost input. Use code to grade exact arithmetic and a human reviewer for the reasoning. Report pass rates across repeated runs. [2026 guide](https://www.anthropic.com/research/demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents)
8. **Inspect AI.** An open-source framework from the UK AI Security Institute and Meridian Labs. Use the custom scorer example to build an evaluation from your own task samples and inspect how the model reached the recommendation. Run the same cases against two configurations and compare task-level failures. [Scoring documentation](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/scoring.html) · [Log viewer](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/log-viewer)
9. **Argo-Bench.** The October 2026 preprint and released benchmark evaluate agents on forecasting, finance, and other workflows inside a simulated delivery marketplace. Read the examples and choose one to adapt as a small, interpretable exercise. Grade the business result and the selected metric, alongside the agent's explanation. [Paper and release links](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02122)
10. **BusinessCaseBench.** This 2026 preprint scores model answers to questions drawn from business cases using instructor-derived rubrics. Use the design as inspiration for an original vignette with a scoring rubric. Require learners to defend one assumption and adapt their recommendation when it changes. The benchmark measures model answers to cases. [Project page](https://business-ai-benchmark.github.io/) · [Preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16057)
11. **NIST Generative AI Profile.** Translate the public risk-management guidance into a short review for a proposed AI feature. Assign an owner for evaluation, define evidence required before launch, and specify what will be monitored and escalated after launch. [NIST AI 600-1](https://www.nist.gov/publications/artificial-intelligence-risk-management-framework-generative-artificial-intelligence)

## Follow new research

12. **Scite.** Follow supporting, contrasting, and mentioning citations to a seed paper and inspect the actual citation context. Start with a DOI from the campaign tutorial and record what each subsequent study actually tests. Smart Citation labels are an aid to reading, and some features depend on your plan or institutional access. [Scite features](https://scite.ai/features) · [Access options](https://scite.ai/pricing)
13. **Wharton Generative AI Labs.** Follow the research archive for AI in learning, collaboration, and knowledge work. The October 2026 Wharton adoption report is useful for understanding what surveyed organizations report doing with AI. Pair those self-reports with a field experiment when estimating actual effects. [Research and insights](https://gail.wharton.upenn.edu/research-and-insights/) · [2026 adoption report](https://knowledge.wharton.upenn.edu/special-report/2026-ai-adoption-report/)
14. **Stanford HAI.** Start with the 2026 AI Index's Economy chapter for an annual snapshot of adoption, productivity, and work. Follow the November 2026 AI100 panel report for the broader implications for organizations and education. Use the underlying sources when turning a headline statistic into a teaching claim. [AI Index Economy chapter](https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2026-ai-index-report/economy) · [2026 AI100 report](https://ai100.stanford.edu/reports/2026-report)
15. **NBER Digital Economics and Artificial Intelligence.** The Summer Institute 2026 program links to emerging research on firms, labor, and decision-making. Pick a study with an explicit comparison group and trace the business outcome, assignment unit, and time horizon before using it in a lecture. [2026 program and papers](https://www.nber.org/conferences/si-2026-digital-economics-and-artificial-intelligence)

# People in AI and business analytics

Researchers and practitioners grouped by contribution, with readings published or updated since 2023. For evidence by topic and study design, see the [research guide](RESEARCH.md).

## Which author for which question?

| Question | Author and entry point |
|---|---|
| Where does AI create economic value in a decision? | **Ajay Agrawal, Joshua Gans, and Avi Goldfarb** on how cheaper prediction changes the value of human judgment and creates opportunities for workflow redesign. [Rotman, *The Lasting Lessons of Understanding AI as a Prediction Machine* (2026)](https://www.rotman.utoronto.ca/the-rotman-experience/about-rotman/ai-at-rotman/ai-era-management-matters-more/understanding-ai-prediction-machine/) |
| How do I turn a model score into a business decision? | **Richard Huntsinger** uses classification for customer churn and other operating decisions. Use section 6.4, “Telecom Customer Churn,” to discuss action costs and when to intervene. [Cambridge, *Business Analytics* (2025)](https://www.cambridge.org/highereducation/books/business-analytics/49F97FC7360294F70056ADDC895C61AE) |
| How do I test whether a business intervention works? | **Ron Kohavi** and colleagues on statistical pitfalls in A/B tests. **Susan Athey** and colleagues on choosing interventions that vary across groups. [*Statistical Challenges in Online Controlled Experiments* (2024 issue)](https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.2023.2257237) · [*Policy Learning with Adaptively Collected Data* (2024)](https://www.gsb.stanford.edu/faculty-research/publications/policy-learning-adaptively-collected-data) |
| Where should marketers apply predictive or generative AI? | **Rajkumar Venkatesan and Jim Lecinski**, *The AI Marketing Canvas* for choosing use cases and scaling adoption. **Paul Ellickson** and colleagues give an empirical example of evaluating proposed marketing content. [The AI Marketing Canvas](https://www.darden.virginia.edu/node/34946) · [Marketing study](https://doi.org/10.1177/00222437261476639) |
| How should people work with generative AI? | **Ethan Mollick**, *Co-Intelligence* for collaboration practices. **Erik Brynjolfsson, Danielle Li, and Lindsey Raymond** for measured effects from a workplace rollout. [Book](https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/741805/co-intelligence-by-ethan-mollick/9780593716717/) · [Field study](https://doi.org/10.1093/qje/qjae044) |
| How do I evaluate an AI workflow before deploying it? | **Shreya Shankar and Hamel Husain** for task-level errors and evaluator checks. **Chip Huyen** for how evaluation, retrieval, and operating cost shape the system. [Evals for AI Engineers](https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/evals-for-ai/9798341660717/) · [AI Engineering](https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/ai-engineering/9781098166298/) |

The [book catalog](BOOKS.md) lists editions, access options, and suggested chapters.

## Business analytics, causal inference, and experimentation

| Person | Contribution to explore | Sources |
|---|---|---|
| **Susan Athey** · Stanford Graduate School of Business | Connects econometrics and machine learning through treatment-effect estimation and policy learning. The 2024 paper studies what happens when the data informing a targeting policy were collected with an adaptive experiment. | [Faculty research and publications](https://www.gsb.stanford.edu/faculty-research/faculty/susan-athey) · [*Policy Learning with Adaptively Collected Data* (2024)](https://www.gsb.stanford.edu/faculty-research/publications/policy-learning-adaptively-collected-data) |
| **Ron Kohavi** | Studies how online experiments support rollout decisions at scale. In a 2026 replication study with colleagues, larger tests found little or no effect of rounded shapes on click-through rates. | [Publications and talks](https://ai.stanford.edu/~ronnyk/) · [*Power Analysis Is Essential* (2026 journal article, author copy)](https://sites.stat.columbia.edu/gelman/research/published/KohaviEtAlMarch2026.pdf) |
| **Richard Huntsinger** · University of California, Berkeley | Presents business cases that connect data cleaning, prediction, and optimization to decisions. The churn case gives readers a concrete setting for discussing how to respond to a model score. | [*Business Analytics: Methods and Cases for Data-Driven Decisions* (2025)](https://www.cambridge.org/highereducation/books/business-analytics/49F97FC7360294F70056ADDC895C61AE) |
| **Stefan Wager** · Stanford Graduate School of Business | Connects causal inference, statistical learning, and decision-making. Read chapters 4 and 5 for estimating who benefits from an intervention and testing the targeting policy that results. | [Faculty profile](https://www.gsb.stanford.edu/faculty-research/faculty/stefan-wager) · [*Causal Inference: A Statistical Learning Approach* (2026 draft)](https://web.stanford.edu/~swager/causal_inf_book.pdf) |

## Text intelligence and marketing

| Person | Contribution to explore | Sources |
|---|---|---|
| **Paul Ellickson** · University of Rochester Simon Business School | Uses quantitative marketing and causal inference to study firm decisions. His co-authored work on novel unstructured treatments combines text representations and historical causal evidence to evaluate proposed marketing content. | [Faculty profile](https://simon.rochester.edu/faculty/paul-ellickson) · [Evaluating Novel Unstructured Treatments with Generative AI](https://doi.org/10.1177/00222437261476639) |
| **Dan Jurafsky** · Stanford University | Co-authors the open *Speech and Language Processing* draft with James H. Martin. The text supplies technical foundations for classifying, representing, and retrieving the unstructured records used in business analytics. | [Research and publications](https://stanford.edu/~jurafsky/) · [Open textbook](https://web.stanford.edu/~jurafsky/slp3/) |
| **Arul Mishra** · University of Utah David Eccles School of Business | Uses machine learning to study consumer decisions. In one co-authored study, the team traced how associations learned from text reached advertisements and recommendations and tested consumer responses. | [Faculty publications](https://profiles.faculty.utah.edu/u0571376/publications) · [Algorithms Propagate Gender Bias in the Marketplace](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcpy.1351) |
| **Himanshu Mishra** · University of Utah David Eccles School of Business | Applies machine learning and computational social science to consumer and marketplace behavior. His co-authored study on LLM-assisted hypothesis generation illustrates a research workflow where language models propose hypotheses for researchers to assess. | [Faculty profile](https://profiles.faculty.utah.edu/u0521228) · [Machine-Assisted Social Psychology Hypothesis Generation](https://doi.org/10.1037/amp0001222) |
| **Rajkumar Venkatesan** · University of Virginia Darden | Studies customer analytics and marketing return on investment. In the second edition of *The AI Marketing Canvas*, he and Jim Lecinski connect predictive and generative AI use cases with adoption and governance. | [Faculty profile](https://www.darden.virginia.edu/faculty-research/directory/rajkumar-venkatesan) · [The AI Marketing Canvas](https://www.darden.virginia.edu/node/34946) |

## Forecasting and operational decisions

| Person | Contribution to explore | Sources |
|---|---|---|
| **Dimitris Bertsimas** · MIT Sloan | Connects statistical learning with optimization. His paper with Lisa Everest and Vasiliki Stoumpou studies how structured and unstructured data can inform treatment recommendations, with outcomes evaluated on historical data. | [Faculty profile](https://mitsloan.mit.edu/faculty/directory/dimitris-bertsimas) · [*Multimodal Prescriptive Deep Learning* (2026)](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=AwfWOCVLbJ) |
| **Rob J. Hyndman** · Monash University | Co-authors *Forecasting: Principles and Practice, the Pythonic Way*. The free book covers seasonal baselines, time-series validation, uncertainty, and forecasts across product or regional hierarchies. | [Research and software](https://robjhyndman.com/) · [*Forecasting: Principles and Practice, the Pythonic Way* (2026)](https://otexts.com/fpppy/) |
| **Warren B. Powell** | Develops frameworks for sequential decisions under uncertainty. His inventory examples show how repeated decisions use forecasts, costs, constraints, and information observed over time. | [*Sequential Decision Analytics and Modeling*, 2nd ed. (2026)](https://warrenpowell.org/sdamodeling/) |

## AI value, work, and organizations

| Person | Contribution to explore | Sources |
|---|---|---|
| **Ajay Agrawal** · University of Toronto Rotman | Studies AI economics and innovation. In work with Joshua Gans and Avi Goldfarb, he explains how cheaper prediction changes the value of judgment and creates opportunities to redesign decisions. | [Faculty profile](https://www.rotman.utoronto.ca/the-rotman-experience/our-community/people/agrawal-ajay/) · [The authors' 2026 update to their prediction framework](https://www.rotman.utoronto.ca/the-rotman-experience/about-rotman/ai-at-rotman/ai-era-management-matters-more/understanding-ai-prediction-machine/) |
| **Erik Brynjolfsson** · Stanford Digital Economy Lab | Studies how digital technology affects productivity and work. His co-authored field paper on a customer-support assistant separates average productivity changes from variation across workers. | [Lab research profile](https://digitaleconomy.stanford.edu/person/erik-brynjolfsson/) · [Generative AI at Work](https://doi.org/10.1093/qje/qjae044) |
| **Karim R. Lakhani** · Harvard Business School | Studies digital transformation and how organizations redesign work around AI. His co-authored consulting experiment reports performance improvements on some tasks and losses on a task outside the tested tool's capabilities. | [Harvard profile](https://www.cityleadership.harvard.edu/about/person/karim-lakhani/) · [Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier](https://doi.org/10.1287/orsc.2025.21838) |
| **Ethan Mollick** · Wharton | Studies generative AI in work, entrepreneurship, and education. His co-authored experiment compares individual and team work with and without AI on product-development tasks. *Co-Intelligence* introduces practical ways for people to work with generative AI. | [Faculty profile](https://knowledge.wharton.upenn.edu/faculty/ethan-mollick/) · [The Cybernetic Teammate](https://doi.org/10.1287/orsc.2025.20702) · [Co-Intelligence](https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/741805/co-intelligence-by-ethan-mollick/9780593716717/) |

## Production AI systems and evaluation

| Person | Contribution to explore | Sources |
|---|---|---|
| **Hamel Husain** | Publishes engineering practices for evaluating AI applications. His practitioner guide turns observed errors into production checks and explains how to assess a model-based grader against human labels. | [Your AI Product Needs Evals](https://hamel.dev/blog/posts/evals/) · [Evals for AI Engineers](https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/evals-for-ai/9798341660717/) |
| **Chip Huyen** | Writes about designing and operating machine learning systems. Her *AI Engineering* book connects evaluation, retrieval, cost, and latency to product architecture. | [Author site](https://huyenchip.com/) · [AI Engineering](https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/ai-engineering/9781098166298/) |
| **Shreya Shankar** | Studies how people specify quality criteria and assess LLM outputs. Her co-authored paper on evaluator alignment examines how human preferences can inform and test automated evaluators. | [Research and publications](https://www.sh-reya.com/) · [Who Validates the Validators?](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~bjoern/papers/shankar-validators-uist2024.pdf) |

# Recent AI in Business Analytics resources

Checked **November 18, 2026**. These books, courses, and practice resources were released or substantially updated in **2025–2026**. The selection emphasizes business decisions, AI workflows, and assignments suitable for a studio. For research papers and benchmarks, see the [state of the art](STATE_OF_THE_ART.md) and [research index](RESEARCH.md).

| Browse | What you will find |
|---|---|
| [Books](#books) | Business analytics, enterprise deployment, retrieval, and evaluation |
| [Open course materials](#open-course-materials) | Teaching examples, project requirements, and practical exercises |
| [Practice and institutional resources](#practice-and-institutional-resources) | Public project briefs, business adoption evidence, and workshop materials |

## Books

### Evals for AI Engineers

**Shreya Shankar and Hamel Husain · O’Reilly · October 2026.** Commercial book with a public contents page. The error-analysis, human annotation, and automated evaluator chapters help studio teams turn observed failures into a grading rubric and repeatable checks. [Publisher and contents](https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/evals-for-ai/9798341660717/)

### Co-Existence

**Ethan Mollick · Portfolio · October 2026.** Commercial book with a public companion site. This follow-up to his 2024 bestseller *Co-Intelligence* is a business-facing read on how people and organizations might work with AI. Pair it with the [field studies](RESEARCH.md#organizations-and-real-work) when assessing productivity or adoption claims. [Publisher](https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/813026/co-existence-by-ethan-mollick/) · [Author companion](https://co-existence.ai/classic/)

### Business Analytics and Artificial Intelligence: Concepts, Skills and Real World Application

**Zabihollah Rezaee, Joseph H. Zhang, Salem Lotfi Boumediene, and Nick J. Rezaee · Routledge · first edition released October 2026, copyright 2027.** Commercial book with a preview. Chapters 6, 8, and 12–14 offer a broad survey of strategy, prescriptive analytics, industry uses, responsible AI, and organizational transformation. For a project on testing agents, pair the survey with the evaluation resources on this page. [Publisher and contents](https://www.routledge.com/Business-Analytics-and-Artificial-Intelligence-Concepts-Skills-and-Real-World-Application/Rezaee-Zhang-Boumediene-Rezaee/p/book/9781041124009) · [Publisher release listing](https://www.routledge.com/economics-finance-business-industry/business-management-and-marketing/research-methods-in-management)

### Speech and Language Processing

**Daniel Jurafsky and James H. Martin · third-edition draft · August 19, 2026 release.** Free online manuscript and selected slides. Chapters 4 and 5 support classification baselines and embeddings. Chapter 11 covers information retrieval and retrieval-augmented generation, useful for a studio project answering questions with source evidence. [Authors’ edition and chapter downloads](https://web.stanford.edu/~jurafsky/slp3/)

### The Agentic Enterprise

**Babak Hodjat and Antoine Blondeau · O’Reilly · July 2026.** Commercial book with a public contents page. Use the chapters on the business case and return on investment to compare build-versus-buy decisions, pilot costs, and the work required to expand a deployment. The enterprise examples provide discussion cases. [Publisher and contents](https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/the-agentic-enterprise/0642572274566/)

## Open course materials

### Product Management · BYU Marriott

**Scott Murff · MSB 341 / IS 693R / CS 498R · Fall 2026, course site published September 14, 2026.** Free course book and assignments. Following its hands-on tooling may require paid access. Use “Models in Your Product” for retrieval, tools, costs, and evals. Use “Measuring What Matters” to connect a product feature to business outcomes. [Course site](https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/) · [Models in Your Product](https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/11-models-in-your-product.html) · [Measuring What Matters](https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/14-measuring-what-matters.html)

### Engineering AI Agents · Stanford

**Diyi Yang, Michael Ryan, and John Yang · CS 329Z · Fall 2026.** Public schedule, selected slides, and project brief. The November 4 session gives students a structure for specifying the task, environment, stopping conditions, and scoring. The November 11 session covers judge design and reliability. The project brief shows how to require evidence that a proposal succeeds in a realistic setting. [Schedule and slides](https://cs329z.stanford.edu/) · [Project brief](https://cs329z.stanford.edu/project.html)

### Marketing Text Analytics · University of Utah Eccles

**Promothesh Chatterjee · MKTG 4640 · Spring 2026.** Public syllabus and project brief. The Yelp restaurant project turns sentiment, topics, and customer segments into recommendations about service, menus, and promotions. It provides a local model for asking students to defend a business decision with evidence from text. [Official syllabus and project](https://class-tools.app.utah.edu/syllabus/1264/12473/MKTG%2B4640%2BSyllabus.pdf#page=8)

## Practice and institutional resources

### Fall 2026 AI & Analytics Accelerator Projects

**Wharton AI & Analytics Initiative · Fall 2026.** Public sponsor briefs. Expedia’s brief asks for an evaluator for agent-generated travel text and images. RxSense’s brief asks students to forecast returns on AI investments. Use either as a model for writing a studio brief with deliverables, evaluation criteria, and a decision owner. The program arranges sponsor data access for participants. [Project briefs](https://ai-analytics.wharton.upenn.edu/for-students/ai-analytics-accelerator/#fall-2026-ai-analytics-accelerator-projects)

### The Adaptive Advantage: Who’s Winning With AI and How

**Wharton Human-AI Research and GBK Collective · October 13, 2026.** Public report summary and download. The survey compares what leaders and employees report about adoption, training, agents, and returns. Use the results to choose survey measures for a case discussion. Pair any effectiveness claim with evidence from a field experiment. [Report and summary](https://knowledge.wharton.upenn.edu/special-report/2026-ai-adoption-report/)

### The Enterprise AI Playbook: Lessons from 51 Successful Deployments

**Elisa Pereira, Alvin Wang Graylin, and Erik Brynjolfsson · Stanford Digital Economy Lab · April 2, 2026.** Free report. Cases of successful implementations show how teams redesigned workflows, tracked value, and assigned human oversight. Use the cases to develop pilot evaluation criteria. The case selection supports learning from successful examples. [Report and PDF](https://digitaleconomy.stanford.edu/publication/enterprise-ai-playbook/)

### Demystifying evals for AI agents

**Mikaela Grace, Jeremy Hadfield, Rodrigo Olivares, and Jiri De Jonghe · Anthropic Engineering · January 9, 2026.** Free engineering guide. Its distinctions between outcome checks and trace inspection are useful for scoring a studio prototype. Give students examples with stale data, incorrect figures, or actions outside their permission. Ask them to define what should happen and build a test for each case. [Engineering guide](https://www.anthropic.com/research/demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents)

### Meridian Open-Source

**Google Meridian team · public release January 29, 2025.** Free open-source library, documentation, and examples. The calibration and budget optimization notebooks offer an applied marketing analytics exercise. Have students explain how experiment inputs influence channel estimates before they recommend a budget. [Release announcement](https://blog.google/products/ads-commerce/meridian-marketing-mix-model-open-to-everyone/) · [Official notebooks](https://developers.google.com/meridian/notebook)

# Research guide

Start with the business claim you want to learn to evaluate. The entries distinguish experiments in operating firms, observational analyses, and benchmarks. See the [research references](REFERENCES.md) for full citations and the [2025–2026 resource shortlist](RECENT_RESOURCES.md) for books, courses, and guides. Citation counts and model benchmark scores answer different questions from a controlled comparison against the current business process.

The [state-of-the-art review](STATE_OF_THE_ART.md) summarizes recent findings across topics. Ellickson is a reference for causal analytics with text, Fang for business outcomes, and Argo-Bench for workflow evaluation. The [campaign tutorial](../labs/01_campaign_decision.ipynb) turns the three ideas into a single synthetic case.

For a closer look at recent evaluation designs, see [analytics methods and research](ANALYTICS_METHODS.md). Use [applied research by function](BUSINESS_APPLICATIONS.md) to find studies tied to a particular operating decision.

## Landmark and widely cited articles

These widely discussed papers from 2023 onward give you contrasting ways to evaluate generative AI in professional work. Citation counts below are Scite's citing-publication counts as checked on **November 18, 2026**. They depend on index coverage and publication age. Use the research design and relevance to decide how much weight to give a result. For regularly published work, see the [journal guide](JOURNALS.md).

| Article | Why researchers read it | Scite citing publications |
|---|---|---:|
| Noy and Zhang (2023), [Experimental Evidence on the Productivity Effects of Generative Artificial Intelligence](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adh2586), *Science* | A preregistered online experiment on selected professional writing tasks that measures time and quality. | 2,547 |
| Brynjolfsson, Li, and Raymond (2025), [Generative AI at Work](https://doi.org/10.1093/qje/qjae044), *The Quarterly Journal of Economics* | Evidence from a staggered deployment of AI support in an operating firm, with effects varying across workers. | 1,341 |
| Dell’Acqua et al. (2026), [Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier](https://doi.org/10.1287/orsc.2025.21838), *Organization Science* | A consulting experiment showing that AI-assisted performance varies with the task. | 343 |

**Management perspective.** The [2026 Wharton adoption report](https://knowledge.wharton.upenn.edu/special-report/2026-ai-adoption-report/) describes what surveyed organizations say they do. Compare this with the observed outcomes in the field studies below.

## Marketing and experimentation

| Source | Evidence | How to read it |
|---|---|---|
| Ellickson et al. (2026), [Evaluating Novel Unstructured Treatments with Generative AI](https://doi.org/10.1177/00222437261476639), *Journal of Marketing Research* | Observational promotion data, causal estimates relying on identification assumptions, and retrospective validation on held-out creatives | Read the empirical context, then the sections on incumbent–challenger decisions and local support. Follow how the analysis handles 34 subject-line treatments and when it recommends more evidence. The new AI-generated copy was scored using predictions. · [Author’s preprint link](https://www.guangzeng.net/research) |
| Fang et al. (2026), [Generative Artificial Intelligence and Sales Productivity](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2026.00623), *Management Science* | Randomized field experiments on seven workflows at one cross-border retailer | Compare the sales outcome and the comparator for each workflow. Report the range from no detectable lift to 16.3%, the role of conversion, and why these sales results alone cannot establish contribution margin. [Author working paper](https://thearf-org-unified-admin.s3.amazonaws.com/MSI/2026/MSI_Report_26-112.pdf) |
| Larsen et al. (2024), [Statistical Challenges in Online Controlled Experiments](https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.2023.2257237), *The American Statistician* | Peer-reviewed review of online A/B testing methods, first published online in October 2023 | Read the sections on long-term effects, sequential testing, and interference. Use them to choose a metric, stopping rule, and randomization unit for an online experiment. |

## Forecasting and operational decisions

| Source | Evidence | How to read it |
|---|---|---|
| Hollmann et al. (2025), [Accurate Predictions on Small Data with a Tabular Foundation Model](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08328-6), *Nature* | Predictive benchmark study across public tabular datasets | Examine benchmark eligibility and compare with capacity-matched baselines on a future-period or group holdout for your business decision. |
| Ansari et al. (2026), [Chronos-2 follow-up](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.41956) | October 2026 preprint on multivariate foundation-model forecasting with covariates | Match the information available to each method, score uncertainty separately, and check how the model's forecasts change a business decision. |
| Liu et al. (2026), [GIFT-Eval-CTX](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.17794) | October 2026 preprint benchmark for contextual forecasting | Check which upcoming events and other context would be available at the time of the forecast. Compare every candidate with a baseline using the same information. |

## Organizations and real work

| Source | Evidence | How to read it |
|---|---|---|
| Brynjolfsson, Li, & Raymond (2025), [Generative AI at Work](https://doi.org/10.1093/qje/qjae044), *The Quarterly Journal of Economics* | Staggered rollout of an assistant to 5,172 customer-support agents | Look at issues resolved per hour and how effects differ by experience. Discuss how to measure quality, escalations, and net benefit alongside throughput in a new deployment. |
| Dell’Acqua et al. (2026), [Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier](https://doi.org/10.1287/orsc.2025.21838), *Organization Science* | Preregistered experiment with BCG consultants on selected tasks | Work through the selected tasks and [Figure 5](https://www.hbs.edu/ris/Publication%20Files/dell-acqua-et-al-2026-navigating-the-jagged-technological-frontier_5c589c8c-fbb5-458f-b285-c944746cd717.pdf#page=12). One difficult task showed roughly a 19-percentage-point average drop in correctness across GPT-4 conditions versus the control. |
| Dell’Acqua et al. (2026), [The Cybernetic Teammate](https://doi.org/10.1287/orsc.2025.20702), *Organization Science* | Preregistered product-innovation experiment with 791 P&G professionals | Compare individuals and teams with and without AI. Focus on whether expert evaluators judged the proposed solutions stronger, then identify which business outcomes would require follow-up. |
| Hosanagar and Ahn (2026), [Designing Human and Generative AI Collaboration](https://doi.org/10.1093/pnasnexus/pgag353), *PNAS Nexus* | Experiment comparing three ways to divide work between people and AI on a 1,000-word creative writing task | Completion times were similar. The design that gave AI the lead and left people to approve or reject its work showed lower quality, satisfaction, and creative diversity. Use the measures to compare who leads different stages of a studio workflow. |
| Otis et al. (2026), [The Uneven Impact of Generative AI on Entrepreneurial Performance](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.06909), *Management Science* | Field experiment on GPT-4 business advice for entrepreneurs in Kenya | Look at the average result and how it varies across businesses. Use this to practice designing a pilot that can learn whom an assistant helps and what advice can backfire. |
| Choi and Xie (2026), [Human + AI in Accounting](https://doi.org/10.1111/1475-679X.70052), *Journal of Accounting Research* | Survey and usage records, plus a randomized framed experiment in transaction classification | In the experiment, 99 accountants classified 43 anonymized transactions. Compare the accuracy and time results with the errors that arose when suggestions were less accurate, then design a review rule. |
| Barwick et al. (2026), [AI as Shared Business Infrastructure](https://doi.org/10.3386/w36003), *NBER Working Paper 36003* | Matched difference-in-differences on one Chinese e-commerce platform | The estimated 51.6% monthly sales increase applies to firms with annual sales below RMB 5 million in the setting studied. Inspect the comparison and pre-trends before transferring the estimate. The working paper was checked at NBER. |
| Kim, Kim, and Koning (2026), [Mapping AI into Production](https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6513481), *INSEAD Working Paper 2026/20/STR* | Field experiment with 515 high-growth startups | The treatment provided examples of how other firms reorganized production around AI. Compare how firms in the two groups discovered uses. The experiment tests guidance about where to apply AI within a broader program that supplied AI access. |
| Chatterji et al. (2026), [How Organizations Use AI](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2608.12236) | Preprint using privacy-preserving ChatGPT Enterprise usage records through March 2026 | Use the study to identify real tasks and adoption differences across functions. Data from a single provider describe usage patterns. To establish downstream productivity, design an additional comparison. |

## Evaluation and governance

| Source | Evidence | How to read it |
|---|---|---|
| Tomitsuka et al. (2026), [Argo-Bench](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.02122) | Preprint benchmark with 210 tasks in a simulated enterprise | Compare data retrieval, analysis, and decision quality. The strongest tested configuration earned at least 95/100 on 34.8% of tasks. Read examples of apparently careful analysis applied to the wrong quantity or objective. |
| Zhao et al. (2026), [BizAgentBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20424v3) | Preprint benchmark, November 5 revision, with 50 tasks based on payments workflows | Compare goal attainment with validity of intermediate steps. Examine how the agent applied rules with different effective dates and scopes. |
| Poeltl et al. (2026), [MBABench-2.0](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.31711) | October 2026 preprint benchmark with 101 tasks that build financial spreadsheets from scratch | Study the rubric for accuracy, readability, maintainability, and auditability. The best pass rate in their tested configurations was 16%. |
| Patel et al. (2026), [Frontier AI Performance Across the Business Disciplines](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2607.16057) | Preprint benchmark of open-ended case questions in 18 business disciplines | Compare partial credit with full rubric completion. Adapt the scoring idea to a teaching exercise where students have to defend and test their own recommendation. |
| Emett et al. (2026), [The Development of a Generative Artificial Intelligence Governance Framework](https://doi.org/10.2308/horizons-2025-056), *Accounting Horizons* | Governance framework developed through design-science research | Turn one high-risk scenario into control objectives, owners, escalation rules, and an audit trail. Compare the framework with the [NIST Generative AI Profile](https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.AI.600-1). |

## A reusable reading worksheet

For each paper, answer these questions before adding its finding to a presentation.

1. What is the business decision and the unit studied?
2. What does the study compare with the AI-assisted alternative?
3. How do the outcome, time horizon, and economic metric differ?
4. Which claim follows from the study design? Which assumption would break it?
5. What would you test before using the finding in another team or population?

See [online research sources](ONLINE.md) for continuing coverage. Recheck publication versions before reusing evidence.

# State of the art in AI and business analytics

**Evidence reviewed November 18, 2026.** This snapshot focuses on research published or released since January 2025. It distinguishes experiments in firms, observational studies, and evaluations of systems. The [full research references](REFERENCES.md) give publication details. The [recent resource shortlist](RECENT_RESOURCES.md) covers books, courses, and guides. For a specific problem, use the [topic index](../learning/TOPIC_INDEX.md). For sources to keep up with new work, see the [research feeds](ONLINE.md#follow-new-research) and [people directory](PEOPLE.md).

## What is established and what is advancing

| Area | Established practice | Research frontier | What to verify for a real decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Data and business intelligence** | Define grain, join keys, time windows, and metric denominators. Reconcile dashboard measures against source records. | Copilots combine SQL, calculations, and retrieval across tables and documents. The DataSpace benchmark scores whether data agents return a complete, verifiable tabular result from a heterogeneous workspace. | Test which metric, period, and entities an assistant selected. Verify intermediate counts and trace important figures to their source. [Star-schema guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/guidance/star-schema) · [DataSpace preprint](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2608.03451) |
| **Tabular prediction** | Use interpretable rules or logistic models as baselines, then compare tree ensembles or other learners on a realistic holdout. Evaluate calibration and the decision threshold as well as ranking. | Recent benchmarks test pretrained tabular models against tuned tree models. The TabPFN-3.5 authors report comparisons that include temporal and grouped data splits. | Use a holdout reflecting the future population and the data available at decision time. Compare cost-weighted errors and how gains change across cohorts. [TabPFN study](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08328-6) · [TabPFN-3.5 technical report, September 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17895) · [Decision economics references](BOOKS.md#business-decisions-and-graduate-analytics) |
| **Forecasting and optimization** | Compare seasonal baselines and tuned models on historical forecast origins. Use uncertainty and asymmetric costs to choose an order, allocation, or staffing level. | Multivariate time-series foundation models can use related series and external inputs. Contextual forecasting benchmarks examine whether models use forward-looking information such as planned events. | Use identical horizons and information for every model. Check calibration and evaluate the downstream policy on stockouts, costs, or service levels. [Chronos-2 follow-up preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.41956) · [GIFT-Eval-CTX preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.17794) · [Inventory lab](../labs/02_inventory_decision.py) |
| **Experiments and causal ML** | Use randomized assignment where feasible. Define the treatment, comparator, estimand, guardrails, and economic threshold before looking at the result. For observational designs, justify identification. | Researchers combine historical causal evidence with embeddings to evaluate new actions described in text. A recent digital experimentation roundtable discusses using experimental, observational, and synthetic evidence for different questions. | Put effect heterogeneity and support on the same footing as model fit. Validate on completely held-out treatments and collect new evidence for actions far from the ones observed. [Ellickson et al.](https://doi.org/10.1177/00222437261476639) · [November 2026 roundtable preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16335) · [Campaign lab](../labs/01_campaign_decision.ipynb) |
| **Text, customer research, and retrieval** | Build an auditable classification or extraction baseline. Validate labels against human examples. For question answering, retrieve policy or document evidence that applies to the user and time period. | The Wharton–Petco case combines text and image analytics with retrieval for email drafting. A separate synthetic-respondent preprint found that aggregate agreement with human responses could mask weak respondent-level discrimination. | Match validation to the decision. Audit subgroup and item-level errors, source dates, claim support, and whether the system abstains when evidence is missing. [Wharton–Petco case](https://ai-analytics.wharton.upenn.edu/student-programs/analytics-accelerator/optimizing-petcos-email-marketing-strategy-using-generative-ai/) · [Netzer and Sambandam preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.13995) · [Grounded Q&A lab](../labs/03_grounded_policy_qa.py) |
| **Agents and workflow evaluation** | Separate reading data, calculating, drafting, acting, and approving. Grade exact business checks in code where possible and review trade-offs separately. | Recent benchmarks evaluate work products and how an agent carries out a task. BizAgentBench records whether intermediate actions follow policy, and MBABench-2.0 tests the auditability and usefulness of financial spreadsheets. | Report full-task pass rates, failure categories, and results across repeated runs. A correct answer can coexist with bad actions or unsupported evidence. [BizAgentBench, November revision](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20424v3) · [MBABench-2.0 preprint](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.31711) · [Agent evaluation guide](https://www.anthropic.com/research/demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents) |
| **Business value and deployment** | Compare with the incumbent workflow. Account for integration and human review, operational errors, adoption, permissions, monitoring, and rollback. | Recent field experiments measure outcomes in operating businesses. Usage studies describe tasks and adoption. Governance research offers ways to design and document controls. | Measure outcomes on both sides of the decision, such as resolution and repeat contact. Track total costs, risk, who benefits, and whether results persist. [Research on organizations and work](RESEARCH.md#organizations-and-real-work) · [NIST Generative AI Profile](https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.AI.600-1) |

## November 2026 findings

- **Sales outcomes in a controlled comparison.** Fang et al. randomized interventions across seven workflows at one cross-border retailer. Short-run sales effects ranged from no detectable change to 16.3%, with gains mainly through conversion. Compare each workflow with its own incumbent. Estimate margin and rollout costs separately. [*Management Science*, November 6, 2026](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2026.00623)
- **How people and AI divide work.** Hosanagar and Ahn compared three collaboration designs in a creative-writing experiment. Completion times were similar. When AI led and people approved or rejected its output, quality, satisfaction, and creative diversity were lower. Use these outcomes to design a studio comparison of different approval and editing responsibilities. [*PNAS Nexus*, November 10, 2026](https://doi.org/10.1093/pnasnexus/pgag353)
- **Firm outcomes from a platform rollout.** Barwick et al. estimate 51.6% higher monthly sales after adoption among firms with annual sales below RMB 5 million on one Chinese e-commerce platform. This is a matched difference-in-differences estimate for a specific group of firms. The intervention, unit of analysis, and identifying assumptions differ from Fang et al.'s randomized workflow tests. [NBER working paper, November 2026](https://doi.org/10.3386/w36003)
- **Agent outcomes and acceptable execution.** Zhao et al. test 50 tasks based on payments workflows. In one reported model configuration, goal attainment was 42.0% and strict success was 32.7% when the rubric also required valid execution. For a studio project, grade the result, the applicable evidence, and the actions separately. [BizAgentBench preprint, November 5 revision](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20424v3)

## Related evidence from 2025 and 2026

- **Kim, Kim, and Koning, workflow redesign.** In a field experiment with 515 startups, the treatment group learned how other firms reorganized production around AI. The authors report increased discovery of AI use cases, with revenue gains concentrated toward the top of the distribution. The randomized comparison concerns guidance about where to apply AI within a program that gave firms access to AI tools. [INSEAD working paper, 2026](https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6513481)
- **Poeltl et al., financial spreadsheets.** MBABench-2.0 tests 101 spreadsheet construction tasks and grades accuracy, auditability, readability, and maintainability. The best tested configuration passed 16% under the benchmark rubric. Use the criteria to assess a studio deliverable alongside its arithmetic. [MBABench-2.0 preprint, October 22, 2026](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.31711)
- **Brynjolfsson, Li, and Raymond, customer support.** A staggered rollout to 5,172 agents yielded a 15% average increase in issues resolved per hour, with substantial variation across workers. For a similar deployment, measure resolution quality and any work transferred to reviewers. [*The Quarterly Journal of Economics*, 2025](https://doi.org/10.1093/qje/qjae044)
- **Dell’Acqua et al., consulting.** In a preregistered experiment with 758 consultants, GPT-4 improved speed and quality on selected tasks. On one difficult exercise, correctness was approximately 19 percentage points lower when pooling the GPT-4 arms against control. Figure 5 shows why a system needs checks for particular tasks and failure modes. [*Organization Science*, 2026](https://doi.org/10.1287/orsc.2025.21838) · [Figure 5](https://www.hbs.edu/ris/Publication%20Files/dell-acqua-et-al-2026-navigating-the-jagged-technological-frontier_5c589c8c-fbb5-458f-b285-c944746cd717.pdf#page=12)
- **Choi and Xie, accounting.** In a randomized framed experiment, 99 accountants classified 43 anonymized transactions. AI suggestions improved accuracy and efficiency on average, and less accurate suggestions could mislead participants. Separate survey and usage records describe how accountants use assistance in the field. [*Journal of Accounting Research*, 2026](https://doi.org/10.1111/1475-679X.70052)
- **Tomitsuka et al., data agents.** On Argo-Bench, the strongest tested configuration earned at least 95/100 on 34.8% of 210 tasks. The study measures performance in a simulated food-delivery operation. Its error analysis includes cases where the agent used the wrong quantity or objective. [October 2026 preprint](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.02122#S3)
- **Patel et al., business cases.** On BusinessCaseBench, Claude Sonnet 4.6 earned 88.4% average rubric credit and met every criterion on 49.6% of questions. These are measures of model performance on supplied case questions. The scoring design is useful when deciding what a business recommendation must demonstrate. [BusinessCaseBench preprint, v5](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.16057v5#S3)

## How this review was updated

The November 18 search used Scite for recent work on firm outcomes, marketing applications, and workflow benchmarks, then checked candidate DOIs and read available study text or primary abstracts. Recent entries were selected for their connection to a business decision, explicit comparison or evaluation design, and traceable results. The NBER working paper by Barwick et al. was checked at NBER because Scite had yet to index it when searched. The [research references](REFERENCES.md) identify publication types and stable links.

## Questions the evidence leaves open

- **Value outside the pilot.** Which gains survive broader adoption, a longer horizon, changing demand, and full implementation costs? Study the existing process and measure quality, work shifted to reviewers, and the cost of mistakes.
- **Transfer across populations.** Do a model's forecasts, recommendations, or estimated effects hold for new stores, customers, or policies? Choose holdouts that match the proposed change and monitor performance by cohort.
- **Delegation and controls.** Which steps should software execute and which should a person verify? Evaluate both the recommended decision and any actions the system can take.
- **Learning with AI.** When a student uses AI to write a case answer, can they defend its assumptions, recreate the key calculation, and revise their decision when new evidence arrives? Give those skills their own measures. See the [business-school teaching map](../learning/TEACHING_MAP.md).

The [research catalog](RESEARCH.md) has more field studies, methods papers, and a worksheet for reading evidence. The [course](COURSES.md) and [book](BOOKS.md) catalogs point to material for learning the methods and comparing their assumptions.
